chapters.title: Chapter 401 -401-An Invitation from the Chaos Humans
paragraphs: The Chaos Star Sea!
In Daniel’s eyes, it was an extraordinarily high-level grinding zone.
The entry threshold alone was enough to eliminate the overwhelming majority of living beings.
Only those at the peak of the Divine-grade or above possessed the strength to traverse its endless expanse.
Hidden within this sea of stars were countless powerhouses and unimaginable treasures.
Every being capable of surviving here stood among the absolute elite of their respective universes.
It would be a lie to say Daniel had never been tempted by this place.
For a long time, he had planned to thoroughly explore the Chaos Star Sea once he had the time.
Unfortunately, there was simply too much on his plate.
The system’s current quest chain was relentless.
The moment one mission ended, another immediately followed.
Treasure hunting and exploring ancient secrets would have to wait.
There was, however, one thing he knew with absolute certainty.
The final reward for this quest chain was a Universe Fragment.
No matter what happened...
That was a treasure he absolutely had to obtain.
Outside the Chaosverse, a massive tide of refugees had already formed.
Wave after wave of living beings poured outward.
No one cared about factions.
No one cared about allegiances.
Every single survivor shared only one thought—
Get as far away from that cosmic meat grinder as possible.
Inside the Chaosverse itself...
The fighting had long since reached an unimaginable scale.
The forces of the Chitin Universe attacked with savage ferocity, forcing the mortal enemies known as the Order Faction and the Chaos Faction to temporarily unite against their common invader.
What had once been a conflict between two rival factions had evolved into a full-scale war between two entire universes.
The scale of the conflict was beyond comprehension.
Battles involving over a thousand Oracle-grades were now considered nothing more than localized skirmishes.
During the largest engagement so far...
More than ten thousand Oracle-grades had been deployed by both sides combined.
Ten thousand Oracle-grades.
That single number had nearly exhausted the entire military strength of both universes.
It also shattered every historical record for the largest gathering of Oracle-grades ever seen in battle.
Hundreds of Oracle-grades perished during that campaign alone.
Thousands more retreated bearing wounds that would likely never heal.
If even Oracle-grades suffered losses on such a scale...
Then the fate of those below them was even more horrifying.
Hundreds of millions of Divine-grade powerhouses clashed across countless battlefields.
Billions upon billions of quasi-Sages surged forward and fell back like endless tides.
Again and again...
The war shattered every preconceived notion held by the surviving inhabitants of both universes.
A Supreme-grade warrior wasn’t even qualified to be considered cannon fodder here.
At least cannon fodder could delay the enemy for a brief moment.
A Supreme-grade expert would simply disappear the instant they entered the battlefield.
The sheer scale of the war spoke for itself.
By this point...
The conflict had already exceeded what the overwhelming majority of participating forces could endure.
Both sides had simply exhausted themselves.
Neither possessed the strength to continue pressing the offensive.
Taking advantage of this rare lull, countless terrified survivors fled the battlefield.
If they remained any longer...
The next corpse lying upon the battlefield might very well be their own.
Far above the universe...
The mysterious Black Coffin continued its endless struggle against the Bell of Destiny.
The two supreme treasures remained locked in a seemingly eternal stalemate.
Countless living beings silently offered their gratitude toward Lord Sorys.
Had he not restrained the Bell of Destiny...
The Chaosverse would have been sealed completely shut.
There wouldn’t even have been a crack through which anyone could escape.
At every moment...
Starships continuously emerged from the Chaosverse before disappearing into the endless depths of the Chaos Star Sea.
Yet during his entire journey...
Daniel had not encountered a single vessel heading toward the Chaosverse.
His was the only starship sailing alone against the fleeing tide.
As the ships passed one another, the escaping survivors couldn’t help turning to stare.
Their expressions mixed disbelief with utter confusion.
"Has that guy lost his mind?"
"At a time like this... someone actually dares head toward the Chaosverse?"
Their voices carried almost absurd disbelief.
"We’re risking our lives trying to escape..."
"And he’s charging straight inside."
"Heh... there really are all kinds of people in this sea of stars."
"Perhaps that lord possesses enough strength to roam the Chaosverse without fear."
"Whatever..."
"May the stars watch over our lives."
"As long as he doesn’t drag us into whatever madness he’s chasing."
"Forget him."
"Just keep running!"
Before the barrier surrounding the Chaosverse...
The weakened seal created by the clash between the Black Coffin and the Bell of Destiny emitted a faint humming sound.
Activating several Sacred Arts, Daniel infused them throughout his body.
With both hands, he tore open the unstable crack, widening it just enough for passage.
Then he guided the Imperial Bow Ark through the opening.
Once again...
He entered the war-torn universe.
The sight before him was one of complete devastation.
After countless cataclysmic battles, the Chaosverse had become almost unrecognizable.
Wherever Daniel looked, shattered remains of Life Worlds drifted through space.
Broken stars floated silently amid the void.
Entire star systems had been riddled with holes by countless Sacred Arts, leaving behind scenes of heartbreaking destruction.
Many systems had even been drained of every last trace of energy.
Silent.
Lifeless.
Completely devoid of living beings.
It was utterly different from the first time he had arrived.
Back then...
Although the Order Faction and Chaos Faction had fought almost every day, the universe had still possessed an untamed vitality.
It had felt like boiling water—violent, chaotic, yet full of life.
Now...
Only desolation remained.
Comparing the prosperity and order of the Myriad-Star Cosmos with the endless wasteland before him...
The Chaosverse resembled a civilization burned to ashes by eternal war.
It was a forsaken kingdom abandoned even by the gods.
The once-flowing rivers of stars had long since dried into lifeless channels.
The Imperial Bow Ark steadily advanced through the ruined universe.
Suddenly—
Beep!
Beep! Beep!
A series of urgent alerts sounded from one of the communication devices Daniel carried.
He frowned slightly before remembering where it had come from.
It was the communicator Dustin had given him back in the Prosperous Astral Realm.
Its purpose had been to allow members of their group to support one another whenever necessary.
"Dustin?"
Raising an eyebrow, Daniel immediately activated the artifact.
Soon, a familiar voice echoed from within it.
It carried both surprise and delight.
"Faustus?"
"You actually came back?"
Dustin’s astonishment was unmistakable.
"I honestly thought you’d wait until this war was completely over before returning."
"I have a few matters that require my attention here."
Daniel answered calmly.
"By the way..."
"This artifact can also detect the locations of the others?"
"That’s right."
Dustin replied frankly.
"As long as you’re somewhere within the Chaosverse, all of these communicators can sense one another."
"I see."
Daniel nodded in understanding.
"Perfect timing."
Dustin chuckled.
"The Chaos Humans have wanted to invite you over for quite some time."
"We just never found the right opportunity."
"Now that you’ve returned..."
"Would you like to visit our settlement?"
"Oh?"
Daniel fell into thought.
The Chaos Humans...
They were the prehistoric ancestors of humanity from countless civilizations before modern Earth.
The humans of Earth and the Chaos Humans shared the very same origin.
Even today, countless ruins they had left behind remained scattered across Earth.
Long ago, they had ventured into the Endless Starsea.
They first established themselves within the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
Later, after offending a Great Oracle-grade, their Forefather led the entire race away from the Myriad-Star Cosmos and settled within the newly born Chaosverse.
After the passage of countless ages...
The humans of Earth had finally stepped onto the path leading toward the Endless Starsea as well.
Now...
For the first time...
The bloodlines of humanity, separated by countless eras, finally had the opportunity to reunite.

chapters.title: Chapter 402 -402-Gazelle Star System, Meeting Dustin Again
paragraphs: Daniel had no reason to doubt the goodwill of the Chaos Humans.
Back on Earth, Hyman had personally come under the Forefather’s orders to investigate the situation.
Not only had he helped Daniel construct his Divine Domain and gifted him a top-grade Holy Relic, but he had also bestowed a supreme sword manual upon Camille.
Those gifts alone were enough to demonstrate the sincerity of the Chaos Humans.
Besides, Daniel himself was curious about them.
Were these prehistoric people truly the ancient ancestors described in Earth’s legends—those mythical beings said to have split mountains and overturned seas?
Even now, Earth still preserved songs and ancient stone inscriptions recounting their exploits.
Meeting them in person could only be beneficial.
After a moment’s thought, Daniel replied,
"Very well. Send me the coordinates. I’ll head over immediately."
"I’ve already transmitted them."
Dustin’s voice carried a trace of anticipation.
"They’re not too far from your current location."
"Travel safely."
Daniel lowered his gaze toward the communicator.
A blue point marked the location of the Chaos Humans.
Without further hesitation, he altered the Imperial Bow Ark’s course and shot toward the designated coordinates at full speed.
Shattered stars flashed past the observation windows, leaving only fragmented reflections behind.
Though the journey itself wasn’t particularly long, the Ark crossed countless checkpoints and blockade zones along the way.
Fortunately, the Imperial Bow Ark was a Primordial Law Grade flying Sacred Artifact.
Not only was it unimaginably fast, but it also possessed the innate ability to break through dimensional barriers.
Since Daniel had no intention of wasting time, he simply charged straight through every obstacle standing in his path.
Before long...
His vision suddenly opened up.
A remarkably stable river of stars unfolded before him.
Daniel recognized it immediately from the ancient records he had read within the Golden Holy Mountain.
The Wisteria Star River.
The reason the Wisteria Star River had managed to preserve a rare pocket of peace within the war-torn Chaosverse was simple.
Several immensely powerful races that had migrated from other universes had established themselves here.
The Chaos Humans were one of them.
None of those races could be underestimated.
Even the weakest possessed a T7 Oracle-grade powerhouse.
The strongest were protected by T9 Great Oracle-grades.
Although occasional friction existed among the five races internally, they had long since formed an unspoken alliance against all outside threats.
It was precisely that mutual understanding which allowed this region of space to remain relatively peaceful despite the endless wars raging throughout the Chaosverse.
Among those five races, the Chaos Humans controlled several entire star systems.
Their headquarters was located within the Gazelle Star System.
Daniel gazed toward the gradually approaching star system.
Its appearance differed completely from that of the Golden Holy Mountain.
The headquarters of the Golden Holy Mountain consisted of countless layered dimensions personally constructed by various Great Oracle-grades.
It resembled a magnificent palace suspended between overlapping planes of existence, with every corner radiating the profound heritage accumulated over endless ages.
The Gazelle Star System, however, was far more traditional.
It was a conventional stellar realm where commerce and daily life coexisted naturally.
At first glance, it looked remarkably similar to the Black River Star System they had visited previously.
Simple.
Almost ordinary.
Daniel guided the Imperial Bow Ark toward the port.
Whoosh!
A streak of light suddenly flew toward him before stopping in the void ahead.
The light condensed into the figure of a tall young man wearing a mage’s robe.
His features were refined, his bearing composed.
He was a Divine Radiant-grade powerhouse.
The young man carefully examined the Imperial Bow Ark’s appearance and intricate engravings before revealing a warm smile.
"May I ask..."
"Are you Lord Faustus, the leader of our ancestral homeland whom the Chaos Humans have been eagerly awaiting?"
His tone carried exactly the right amount of respect.
Daniel immediately dismissed the Imperial Bow Ark and revealed himself in the open void.
"That’s me."
"Lord Faustus."
"I’ve long admired your reputation."
"The Chaos Humans have already made arrangements for your arrival."
"Please, allow me to escort you."
The young man stepped aside and gestured politely.
"Very well."
Daniel nodded before asking casually,
"What about Dustin?"
"It’s been quite some time since we last met."
"How has he been?"
"Dustin?"
The young man’s lips twitched slightly, as though recalling something amusing.
He looked as if he were trying not to laugh.
"He was summoned to the Hall of Judgment just a little while ago."
"A while back, he ignored direct orders and secretly joined one of the major battles."
"Right now..."
"He’s receiving his punishment."
"Oh?"
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"What exactly happened?"
The young man continued leading the way as he explained.
"Not long ago, when the Chitin Universe launched its all-out invasion of the Chaosverse..."
"The Forefather personally ordered Dustin and the other young prodigies of our race to stay away from the battlefield."
"Their only mission was to continue cultivating and preserve themselves."
He chuckled.
"But Dustin still sneaked out and participated in one of the major engagements."
"In doing so, he directly violated the Forefather’s personal decree."
"He was summoned to the Hall of Judgment."
"And the punishment?"
Daniel asked.
"Is it severe?"
"Nothing too serious."
The young man waved his hand dismissively, still smiling.
"He was merely ordered to reach the Divine Sovereign realm within five hundred years."
Daniel couldn’t help smiling himself.
That counted as punishment?
It sounded far more like an elder giving a promising junior a firm push while setting a clear goal.
It was obvious just how highly Dustin was valued within the Chaos Humans.
The so-called punishment was simply the gentle discipline of a senior guiding the younger generation.
"It seems the Chaos Humans’ Forefather simply doesn’t want the younger geniuses of the clan dying inside that cosmic meat grinder."
Daniel thought to himself.
"After all..."
"The future of the Chaos Humans rests upon these young talents."
"So he would never truly punish Dustin."
From that alone, Daniel could clearly see how much importance the Chaos Humans placed upon nurturing their younger generation.
The atmosphere reminded him strongly of the families back on Earth.
Parents there poured everything they had into raising their children.
As expected of a people who had once originated from Earth...
Even after countless civilization cycles had passed...
The inheritance engraved into their bloodlines remained unmistakable.
Guided by the young man, Daniel gradually entered the inner realms of the Gazelle Star System.
Below them, the distinctive architectural style of the Chaos Humans slowly came into view.
"Originally..."
"It was supposed to be Lord Hyman who welcomed you personally."
"After all, the two of you are already acquainted."
"The Forefather had also planned to meet you himself."
He suddenly paused before letting out a quiet sigh.
Daniel remained perfectly composed, silently waiting for him to continue.
The young man spoke again.
"Both the Forefather and Lord Hyman were injured during the last great battle."
"What?"
Daniel’s expression immediately tightened.
Even the T8 Oracle-grade Forefather had been wounded?
And Hyman had not escaped unscathed either?
The brutality of that war had clearly surpassed everything Daniel had previously imagined.
"The Forefather and Lord Hyman are both currently in seclusion recovering from their injuries."
"I’m afraid they won’t be able to receive you personally."
As he finished speaking, the young man’s smile suddenly widened.
"Look."
"Someone’s coming."
A figure rapidly flew toward them from the distance.
Before even arriving, the newcomer was already waving enthusiastically.
"Faustus!"
"Long time no see!"
The corners of Daniel’s mouth lifted slightly.
That greeting...
Was exactly what he had expected.

chapters.title: Chapter 403 -403-The Twelve Sanctums, the Human Holy See
paragraphs: Dustin looked positively delighted.
The so-called punishment clearly hadn’t weighed on him in the slightest.
In the blink of an eye, he had flown over to Daniel, casually patting him on the shoulder as though they were old friends who had known each other for centuries.
"Dustin, since you’re here, why don’t you take over and show Lord Faustus around?"
The young man smiled as he gladly handed over the responsibility of acting as their guide.
"Just admit you’re looking for an excuse to slack off."
Dustin waved him away without the slightest bit of courtesy before turning back to Daniel with a broad grin.
"Come on, Faustus."
"I’ll show you the territory of the Chaos Humans."
"I’m looking forward to it."
Daniel nodded.
The two of them soon entered the inner realm of the Gazelle Star System.
Wherever Daniel looked, he saw architecture unique to the Chaos Humans.
At a glance, the buildings clearly reflected the style of Earth’s prehistoric civilizations.
Their appearance was rugged and unpretentious, yet closer inspection revealed an astonishing level of craftsmanship hidden within every engraved line and carved pattern.
Each structure carried an indescribable sense of solemnity and reverence, as though the spirit of the ancient ancestors still lingered within the stone itself.
Daniel found himself completely absorbed.
It felt as though he were reading an ancient history book.
The forgotten stories hidden within those pillars and walls seemed to awaken beneath his gaze.
"Next..."
"I’m taking you somewhere special."
"The Twelve Sanctums."
A mysterious gleam flashed through Dustin’s eyes.
The Twelve Sanctums?
Something stirred faintly within Daniel’s heart.
It felt as though an ancient memory buried deep within his mind had been gently touched.
He couldn’t help recalling the ancient legends preserved on Earth.
According to those stories, countless ages ago there had once been twelve sacred halls in the heavens—
The dwelling places of the Creator and the ancient sages.
With Dustin leading the way, the journey proceeded without obstruction.
The two of them ascended higher and higher into the sky.
The scenery suddenly opened into an endless panorama.
A thin veil of glowing mist drifted through the heavens like delicate silk.
For a brief moment, Daniel felt as though he had stepped into one of Earth’s legendary myths.
Beyond the hazy clouds, he could vaguely make out a series of unimaginably magnificent palaces.
They stood silently in the heavens like slumbering giants.
Dustin pointed toward the distant structures.
His tone unconsciously became solemn.
"That..."
"is the Holy See."
The Holy See.
Daniel nodded quietly.
Dustin continued in an even more respectful voice, as though recounting a story passed down through countless generations.
"The Holy See is actually more of a symbol than anything else."
"Long ago..."
"Our Forefather ruled this entire territory under the title of the Holy Emperor."
"It was he who established the Holy See."
"But later..."
"For reasons no one truly understands..."
"He personally dissolved it."
"He returned all governing authority to the Chaos Humans themselves."
"From that day onward, the Holy See no longer stood above ordinary people."
"Everything became governed according to the common laws of the Endless Starsea."
He paused.
"But the Holy See itself wasn’t demolished."
"Because before leaving..."
"The Forefather spoke a single sentence."
Dustin’s eyes grew noticeably deeper.
"He said..."
’The strong always seek to stand above others.’
’They always wish to rule over those beneath them.’
’Yet the highest authority in existence is nothing more than the Will of the World.’
’And even the Will of the World is merely a prisoner held captive by the Great Cosmic Will.’
’If I continue sitting upon the throne of the Holy Emperor...’
’Then how am I any different from a prisoner confined within a cage?’
"He dismissed everyone who served the Holy See."
"He left only this sanctuary behind."
"As a reminder to future generations."
"Never become servants of the Will of the Universe."
"Stay close to the people."
"Use your strength to build a better world for ordinary lives."
"Do not use your strength to oppress those too weak to defend themselves."
"Even the ordinary may one day soar into the heavens."
"As long as hope remains..."
"Anything is possible."
Dustin spoke every word with complete sincerity.
It was obvious that he admired the Human Forefather from the bottom of his heart.
Daniel listened silently.
As he listened, he couldn’t help thinking to himself...
Someone capable of reaching the T8 Oracle-grade truly possessed a vision and breadth of mind far beyond ordinary beings.
"The Holy See is the first level of the Twelve Sanctums?"
Daniel asked.
"Exactly."
Dustin smiled.
"The Holy See is protected by countless formations and seals."
"Normally, no one is permitted to enter except during designated times."
"But you’re different."
Daniel looked at him with slight confusion.
The corners of Dustin’s mouth slowly curled upward into a meaningful smile.
"The Forefather once said..."
"You should enter."
"I should?"
A thought flashed through Daniel’s mind.
He chose not to ask any further questions.
"I simply fly in?"
"That’s right."
Dustin nodded.
Without another word, Daniel shot toward the palace complex hidden within the clouds.
Looking downward, he immediately noticed an invisible barrier surrounding the entire sanctuary.
Whoosh!
He passed through it effortlessly.
Just as Dustin had said...
The Chaos Humans had intentionally granted him permission.
But...
What exactly did they want him to see?
Whoosh—
The instant Daniel stepped onto the grounds of the Holy See—
The scenery before his eyes suddenly transformed.
The sensation was identical to what he had experienced long ago on Aetheria when witnessing the forgotten history of humanity.
In an instant...
His vision was swallowed by endless chaos.
Deep within that boundless chaos floated a magnificent palace.
The entire structure radiated a gentle, ethereal light.
Its brilliance wasn’t dazzling.
Instead, it resembled a full moon that had silently illuminated the world since time immemorial.
Above the palace gates were engraved several solemn words.
Morningstar Temple.
Daniel’s heart suddenly skipped a beat.
That name...
It felt strangely familiar.
He was certain he had encountered it somewhere before.
Yet no matter how hard he searched his memory...
He couldn’t remember where.
Outside the palace stood an ancient hazel tree.
Its emerald branches cascaded downward like a flowing waterfall.
Beneath the tree rested two stone chairs separated by a weathered stone table.
A chessboard had been carved directly into the tabletop.
An elderly man dressed in a mage’s robe sat quietly in one of the chairs.
Between two fingers, he held a bishop chess piece suspended in midair.
For a very long time...
He never placed it upon the board.
His complexion was rosy.
His long robe fluttered gently in the breeze.
Had his eyes not moved from time to time...
Daniel might have mistaken him for nothing more than a stone statue.
The old man frowned as he studied the chessboard before him.
It seemed he had encountered an impossible deadlock.
After what felt like an eternity...
He finally let out a long sigh.
"I, too..."
"Am nothing more than a chess piece in the hands of the Great Cosmic Will."
"How utterly laughable."
With a sudden sweep of his arm—
He scattered every chess piece from the board.
Black and white pieces clattered across the stone floor, rolling in every direction.
The old man slowly rose to his feet.
Then...
He lifted his gaze toward the deepest reaches of the endless chaos.
At that very instant—
Every hair on Daniel’s body stood on end.

chapters.title: Chapter 404 -404-The Origins of the Chaos Humans
paragraphs: The feeling was indescribably strange.
Daniel knew perfectly well that the old man wasn’t looking at him.
Yet it felt as though something invisible had pierced straight through his soul.
It was as if those ancient eyes had crossed the endless river of time itself, falling upon him from an unimaginably distant past...
"Prisoner... chess piece..."
The old man murmured softly.
At that moment, his body suddenly trembled.
Two figures separated from him, one to each side.
All three looked exactly alike.
The only differences lay in their robes and expressions.
The figure on the left wore a pure white mage’s robe.
His expression was gentle, giving off the warmth of a spring breeze gliding across a tranquil lake.
The figure on the right was dressed entirely in black.
His face was cold and emotionless, while a ruthless gleam lingered deep within his eyes.
The old man turned toward the white-robed elder, his voice calm.
"I’m counting on you."
"Even if only a sliver of hope remains, I must gamble everything."
"Otherwise... once those invaders step into this world..."
"It will all be over."
The white-robed elder smiled.
"Leave it to me."
As soon as he finished speaking, his body dissolved into countless motes of light that drifted toward the depths of the world.
Watching him disappear, the old man let out a long sigh.
"The survival and inheritance of a civilization have always been the most important matters."
"If I wish to completely change this world..."
"There is little more I can do."
"I can only remake myself."
"Perhaps then..."
"This civilization may yet find a path to continue."
He slowly turned toward the black-robed elder.
His voice remained as calm as ever.
"Modis."
"I’m about to enter a long slumber."
"The future of this civilization..."
"I leave it in your hands."
The black-robed elder let out a cold laugh.
"Hahaha..."
"You old fool."
"You still think you can use me?"
"I refuse."
"Once you’re asleep..."
"I’ll turn this entire world upside down."
The old man showed no sign of anger.
Instead, a faint smile appeared on his face.
"Everything..."
"Will be judged by time."
The next instant—
Endless currents of the Laws of the Universe surged in like a tidal wave.
Layer upon layer wrapped themselves around his body, sealing him inside an invisible prison.
At the very same moment—
Boom!
The great gates of the Morningstar Temple slowly closed with a deep, resonant rumble.
Daniel silently watched everything unfold.
Like a spectator standing beyond history itself.
He remained upon the riverbank of time, watching its endless current flow before him.
He finally understood.
The master of the Morningstar Temple...
Was none other than the World Will of this universe.
Though he ruled the entire world...
He himself was forever bound by the Great Cosmic Will.
Like a king chained to his own throne.
No matter how magnificent his crown...
He could never overstep his cage.
The old man refused to remain a prisoner forever.
He longed for the countless stars and worlds scattered throughout the Endless Starsea.
Yet the Great Cosmic Will prevented him from growing any stronger.
At the same time, he feared that one day his world would inevitably fall before invading enemies.
So...
He divided himself into two halves.
One of light.
One of darkness.
He sent the benevolent half into the cycle of reincarnation, hoping it would create a new future.
Meanwhile...
The darker half remained behind to govern the world.
It became the crack through which destiny itself might someday be broken.
Daniel immediately grasped the old man’s true intentions.
"This..."
"is the World Will’s final gamble."
"He refused to accept fate."
Whoosh—
The scene before Daniel shifted once again.
The benevolent incarnation was born into an ordinary family.
His name...
Was Aldman.
From birth, Aldman possessed the Sacred Fate Physique.
A quasi-Sage-grade Divine Artifact descended into the world alongside him.
The moment he was born, extraordinary heavenly phenomena filled the skies.
Countless great figures throughout the world were alarmed.
Yet...
As though they had reached a silent agreement...
Every one of them pretended not to have noticed.
Aldman was exceptionally gifted.
Whatever he learned, he mastered almost instantly.
At the age of fifteen, he left home to travel the world.
He first secluded himself within a cathedral for three years.
There, he cultivated a compassionate heart and comprehended his own true path.
During that period, he created a Great Sacred Art—
Radiance of the Sanctum.
Afterward, he entered the Hall of Sages for another three years of secluded cultivation.
There, he forged both a Sacred Heart and Sacred Laws while mastering another Great Sacred Art—
Radiance in a Single Thought.
Later...
He entered the Arcane Academy.
Three years passed once more.
Within those halls, he condensed an Arcane Heart and comprehended the Arcane Laws.
In merely nine years...
He rose to become the supreme existence of that entire world.
Meanwhile...
His evil counterpart, Modis, was hardly idle.
True to his nature, he sowed chaos everywhere he went.
He ignited a catastrophe that swept across the entire world, dragging countless lives into endless warfare.
Yet there was one person he feared above all others—
Aldman.
Therefore...
He deliberately severed the path connecting the Mortal Realm and the Sacred Realm, preventing Aldman’s continued ascension.
But in the end...
Aldman united the strength of all living beings.
With the aid of countless powerful allies, he forcibly shattered the barrier separating the two realms.
He successfully overcame the Sacred Tribulation and ascended to Sagehood.
From that moment onward...
His cultivation advanced at an astonishing pace.
More and more followers gathered beneath his banner.
Eventually...
His strength reached the same level as that of his original self.
Then...
The inevitable battle finally arrived.
Aldman and Modis clashed in a decisive final confrontation.
Aldman emerged victorious.
He slew Modis before ultimately merging with the original body that had remained sealed away.
From that day onward...
The World Will itself was no longer the old man.
It had become Aldman.
He fulfilled the dream he had once envisioned.
Breaking free from the shackles imposed by the Great Cosmic Will...
He led his entire civilization into the Endless Starsea, opening a far broader future for them all.
Many years later...
A remarkably gifted child appeared within the civilization he governed.
His name was Morian.
Morian possessed extraordinary talent.
Aldman personally nurtured him, guiding him step by step until he eventually reached the Oracle-grade.
Yet destiny seldom followed one’s wishes.
During one of his journeys through the Endless Starsea...
Aldman was ultimately slain by a powerful enemy.
With his death...
The once-unified civilization immediately fractured.
The various races gradually drifted apart.
Because Morian had been born a human...
He naturally became the leader of humanity.
At that very time...
An Oracle-grade known as the Emperor Caesar sought to absorb Aldman’s legacy into his own dominion.
After careful consideration...
Most of the other races ultimately chose submission.
Only Morian refused to bow his head.
In doing so...
He directly offended the Emperor Caesar.
Rather than live beneath another’s rule...
Morian led the Chaos Humans away from their homeland.
They journeyed across countless regions before finally settling within the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
Later...
After still more migrations...
They ultimately established themselves inside the newborn Chaosverse.
After enduring countless hardships over the ages...
Morian himself advanced from a T6 Oracle-grade to a T8 Oracle-grade.
Daniel quietly watched every scene unfold.
Only after the final image faded away did the surrounding world gradually return to the appearance of the Holy See.
He slowly blinked, carefully organizing everything he had witnessed.
"This is the true origin of humanity."
"The Chaos Humans came from the Old World."
"That ancient civilization contained countless races."
"After Forefather Aldman fell in battle..."
"It eventually splintered apart."
"Forefather Morian, being human, had originally been chosen by Forefather Aldman as his successor."
"But the other races refused to accept him."
"That was where the first cracks appeared."
"It was because they failed to remain united..."
"That the Emperor Caesar found an opportunity to force them into submission."
"Rather than live under someone else’s rule..."
"Forefather Morian led the human race away while he was still only a T6 Oracle-grade."
"He brought the Chaos Humans into the Chaosverse."
"They endured unimaginable hardship..."
"Until he finally reached the T8 Oracle-grade."
"The road the Chaos Humans have walked..."
"Has truly been a difficult one."
Daniel slowly let out a long breath.
"Why are they treating me so differently?"
"They deliberately granted me access to all of this..."
"Just so I could witness the entire history of the Chaos Humans?"
As he pondered the question—
Suddenly—
Buzz!
Ripples spread across the empty space before him.
An object slowly emerged from the center of the distortion.

"That was where the first cracks appeared."
"It was because they failed to remain united..."
"That the Emperor Caesar found an opportunity to force them into submission."
"Rather than live under someone else’s rule..."
"Forefather Morian led the human race away while he was still only a T6 Oracle-grade."
"He brought the Chaos Humans into the Chaosverse."
"They endured unimaginable hardship..."
"Until he finally reached the T8 Oracle-grade."
"The road the Chaos Humans have walked..."
"Has truly been a difficult one."
Daniel slowly let out a long breath.
"Why are they treating me so differently?"
"They deliberately granted me access to all of this..."
"Just so I could witness the entire history of the Chaos Humans?"
As he pondered the question—
Suddenly—
Buzz!
Ripples spread across the empty space before him.
An object slowly emerged from the center of the distortion.

chapters.title: Chapter 405 -405-Ring of Destiny
paragraphs: It was a ring.
The circular ring was roughly the size of a basketball. Ancient runic patterns were engraved across its surface, their weathered grooves bearing the unmistakable marks of countless ages.
Daniel studied it for a long while, yet he couldn’t determine what it actually was.
It simply hovered silently before him.
If one called it a Divine-grade treasure, it didn’t quite fit.
If it was a construct born from the Laws, that didn’t seem right either.
As for calling it a Sacred Art—that was even less likely.
And yet...
It somehow seemed to combine the strengths of all three while belonging to none of them.
It simply floated there, swaying gently in midair.
Could this... actually be meant for me?
The thought crossed Daniel’s mind as he slowly reached out.
The instant he raised his hand—
Whoosh!
The ring shot forward of its own accord and landed directly in his palm.
The sensation was oddly familiar.
Like a bird that had flown for countless miles before finally finding a branch upon which to rest.
It settled quietly into his hand.
Daniel weighed it gently.
It felt almost weightless, as though he were holding nothing more than a pocket of air.
Lowering his gaze, he inspected it carefully.
Immediately, a panel appeared before his eyes.
[Ring of Destiny (???)]
Category: ???
Special: ???
Effects: ???
Description: ???
An entire screen filled with question marks.
The corner of Daniel’s mouth twitched.
What was going on?
The system had handed him an item with absolutely no explanation whatsoever—aside from its name.
Daniel blinked.
Instead of disappointment, excitement welled up inside him.
The less he could understand something...
The more extraordinary it was likely to be.
"Ring of Destiny..."
he murmured softly.
Judging from the name alone, it was undoubtedly connected to the Law of Destiny and Reincarnation.
After a brief hesitation, Daniel activated True Sight, hoping to uncover at least a fragment of its secrets.
Boom!
An overwhelming torrent of information exploded into his consciousness.
Daniel’s eyes widened instantly.
An uncontrollable surge of exhilaration flooded his heart.
Wait...
No...
This... this is the highest level of the Law of Destiny and Reincarnation!
My luck is unbelievable!
His eyes sparkled.
To him, this treasure was nothing short of timely salvation.
The information contained within regarding the Law of Destiny and Reincarnation alone was already priceless.
Any Divine-grade expert cultivating the Law of Reincarnation would go mad with envy if they learned of it.
The very foundation of Daniel’s Supreme Sage Template was the Law of Reincarnation.
Although the reincarnation laws contained within the template had already reached the Ultimate Grade...
That power had been granted directly by the system.
He could wield it effortlessly...
Yet he had never truly understood its principles or essence.
For a very long time, he had attempted to comprehend it through his own efforts.
Progress, however, had been painfully slow.
After countless years of study...
He had barely managed to reach the beginner level.
Yet merely touching the Ring of Destiny had instantly granted him an incredibly complete understanding of the Law of Destiny and Reincarnation.
The endless stream of knowledge unfolded before him like an ancient scroll opening across the ages.
Every detail...
Every mystery...
Every principle...
Appeared with crystal clarity.
Daniel’s heart pounded with excitement.
With the Ring of Destiny in his possession...
Given enough time to study it...
He was confident that his mastery of the Law of Destiny and Reincarnation would soon advance to the Mid Grade.
For the moment...
He no longer cared why the ring had appeared.
Nor why it had chosen him.
Within one of the layers of the Twelve Sanctums.
A simple wooden cabin stood quietly within a secluded valley.
Several ancient trees grew before its entrance.
Beneath their shade...
Forefather Morian slowly opened his eyes.
A trace of unmistakable astonishment flashed across them.
He had never expected...
That it would be that object.
Originally, his plans for Faustus had been gradual.
If the young man proved worthy of cultivation...
Then he would allocate more resources to him.
If Faustus demonstrated exceptional brilliance...
Then he would open the Legacy Vault and allow its treasures to choose their own master.
Given the current situation...
Faustus had undoubtedly earned that qualification.
After defeating Dustin and standing unrivaled among his peers...
He deserved entry into the vault.
But what Morian never expected...
Was that the treasure which emerged from within...
Would be the very item that even he himself had never dared to touch lightly.
His emotions became exceedingly complicated.
Faustus was even more monstrous than he had imagined.
Before even reaching the Divine-grade...
He had already stood at the absolute summit of his generation.
During the Starlight Tournament...
He single-handedly crushed every genius of the Myriad-Star Cosmos until none could raise their heads.
Even Dustin—the strongest Quasi-Sage of the current generation among the Chaos Humans—
Had been effortlessly defeated by him.
After Chaosverse had been sealed...
Not a single living being had managed to break through its barriers.
Yet Faustus had forcibly torn open a path and advanced into the Divine Sovereign Realm.
Finding even the slightest flaw within the power of an Eternal Sage...
Was something no living being had ever dared imagine.
Yet...
Faustus had accomplished exactly that.
This...
Was true invincibility.
Genuine invincibility.
Complex emotions filled Morian’s eyes.
At every single Rank...
Faustus had become the strongest of his generation.
Even throughout the endless history of the Endless Starsea...
There had only ever been a handful of individuals like him.
Gradually...
Morian felt a measure of comfort.
Though losing the Ring of Destiny pained him somewhat...
His satisfaction far outweighed his regret.
As long as Faustus continued to grow stronger...
Then the seed planted today would someday return rewards countless times greater.
Besides...
The Ring of Destiny had slumbered for countless ages.
It also carried an unimaginably heavy karma.
So heavy...
That even the Chaos Humans could not bear its consequences.
At this point...
There was likely only one person left alive who knew the ring’s true secret.
Morian let out a quiet sigh.
It carried a loneliness he had never been able to share.
Back then...
Forefather Aldman had still been only a T7 Oracle-grade when he ventured into an ancient forbidden land.
Within those forgotten ruins...
He discovered the Ring of Destiny.
To seize it...
He slaughtered every powerful expert present.
But he himself paid an enormous price.
His very foundation was gravely damaged.
He was afflicted by an extremely vicious curse.
From that day onward...
His condition steadily deteriorated.
He secretly brought the Ring of Destiny back to the clan.
He told no one.
Only at the very end of his life...
Did he summon Morian to his bedside.
"Morian..."
"This is the Ring of Destiny."
"From this day forward..."
"It shall be entrusted to your care."
It was Morian’s very first encounter with the ring.
Standing beside Aldman’s bed...
He stared at the rune-covered circle.
No matter how carefully he examined it...
He couldn’t understand what it truly was.
It resembled both a treasure and a construct born from the Laws.
By then...
Morian himself was already an Oracle-grade.
Yet even he could not perceive the profound mysteries hidden within it.
Aldman wasn’t surprised by his confusion.
He merely smiled.
"This..."
"is actually a Holy Spirit."
"It is an obsession..."
"One that slowly evolved over countless ages."
His eyes suddenly shone with unusual brilliance.
"It belongs to an Eternal Sage."
"An Eternal Sage who has already fallen."
"The most important part is..."
"It will never develop a new consciousness."
"It is nothing more than a frozen obsession."
"Like an insect forever sealed inside amber."
"Within it remains only an echo..."
"One left behind by someone who departed long ago."
Aldman instructed Morian to preserve the Ring of Destiny as the clan’s greatest treasure.
Yet there was one warning...
One instruction he repeated again and again.
The ring must never be shown casually to anyone.
Nor could anyone ever learn where it had come from.
Otherwise...
It would bring about a calamity capable of exterminating the entire Chaos Human race.

chapters.title: Chapter 406 -406-The Key to an Eternal Legacy
paragraphs: "I understand."
"I’ll guard this secret with my life."
Back then, Morian had felt a chill run down his spine.
An Eternal Sage.
That was an existence standing at the absolute pinnacle of the Endless Starsea.
Yet the Ring of Destiny had been born from the lingering obsession left behind after such a being had fallen.
No wonder Forefather Aldman had waited until his final moments before entrusting it to him.
The weight of such an item was far beyond what ordinary beings could bear.
If the powerful races of the Endless Starsea ever discovered its existence, the Chaos Humans would face an unimaginable catastrophe.
After Aldman passed away, Morian sealed the Ring of Destiny deep within the innermost chamber of the Legacy Vault.
He never revealed its origin to anyone.
Through countless ages, the treasure remained asleep in the darkness...
Like a forgotten star whose very name had long since faded from memory.
Yet today...
When Faustus entered the Legacy Vault to receive its gifts...
The very first treasure to fly toward him was the most precious one of all—
The sacred spirit born from an Eternal Sage.
At that moment, Morian’s emotions were indescribably complicated.
Daniel stored the Ring of Destiny inside his inventory.
Truthfully, he wanted nothing more than to remain there and carefully study the Laws contained within it.
But he forcibly restrained himself.
Without lingering any longer, he immediately left the Holy See.
After all, he was here as a guest.
Remaining inside someone else’s sacred sanctuary for too long would have been rather impolite.
Seeing Daniel emerge so quickly, Dustin blinked in surprise.
"You’re out already?"
Daniel was briefly taken aback before quickly realizing why.
The Holy See contained a temporal formation.
Although he had experienced a considerable amount of time inside...
Only a short while had passed in the outside world.
Smiling, he replied,
"I’ve already received a rather nice gift."
Dustin shook his head with a laugh.
"You’re far too modest."
"Since Forefather opened the Legacy Vault for you, even the worst treasure inside would be a Primordial Law Grade artifact."
"With your talent and luck, you should have obtained at least a Primordial Supreme Treasure."
"’Rather nice’? I don’t believe that for a second."
Daniel simply smiled without explaining further.
"By the way," he asked, "why did Forefather allow me to enter the Legacy Vault?"
"You didn’t know?"
Dustin grinned.
"That’s been a tradition among the Chaos Humans for countless generations."
"Oh?"
"The Chaos Humans preserve our rarest Sacred Artifacts and supreme treasures within the Legacy Vault."
"Whenever a younger generation worthy of cultivation appears..."
"The vault opens its doors."
"I see..."
Daniel nodded before asking,
"But I’m not actually a member of the Chaos Humans."
"You came from our ancestral homeland."
"Although we now belong to different universes..."
"Our roots are one and the same."
"And besides..."
"No matter where someone comes from, as long as they embrace our civilization and ideals..."
"They’re even eligible to become a candidate to lead the Chaos Humans."
Daniel froze for a moment.
"You mean..."
"I could become the successor of the Chaos Humans?"
Dustin spread his hands.
"Why not?"
"Even among the countless worlds under our rule..."
"It doesn’t matter whether someone is human."
"As long as they can carry forward our civilization and ideals..."
"They have every right to inherit them."
Daniel slowly nodded as he pondered those words.
This principle possessed remarkable vision.
It transcended race and bloodline altogether.
Instead...
It elevated civilization itself above everything else.
A trace of pride appeared in Dustin’s eyes.
"The Chaos Humans didn’t survive this long by luck."
"Our Forefathers all understood one truth."
"No race in the Endless Starsea remains prosperous forever."
"If you want a civilization to endure eternally..."
"You have to keep your doors open."
"Take what is worthy."
"Discard what is not."
"If some extraordinary genius from one of our subordinate races possesses the potential to become an Eternal Sage..."
"And we choose to suppress them simply because they aren’t human..."
"We wouldn’t just make an enemy of a future supreme powerhouse."
"We’d also lose a potential ally."
After a brief pause, Dustin continued,
"So rather than rejecting them..."
"We choose to welcome them."
"We influence them with our civilization."
"As long as they acknowledge our ideals..."
"They won’t harm the Chaos Humans."
"They’ll strengthen us instead."
"That’s why every world ruled by the Chaos Humans is governed through fairness and equality."
"Even the non-human races enjoy the same status as humanity."
Daniel nodded thoughtfully.
He was already considering whether the Humans of Earth should one day adopt many of the Chaos Humans’ institutions and ideals.
Such broad-mindedness...
Was the true foundation that allowed a civilization to survive countless ages.
Suddenly Dustin smiled.
"Come on."
"I’ll show you another place."
"Where?"
"The Trial Grounds inside the Twelve Sanctums."
"There are countless trials there designed to temper one’s will and combat ability."
"There are plenty of good rewards waiting inside."
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Soon afterward, the two of them passed through layer after layer of sacred domains before arriving at a vast, tranquil expanse.
The air itself carried an ancient, solemn atmosphere.
At the center of the grounds stood two enormous stone monuments.
One was black.
The other white.
They stood opposite one another like the boundary between day and night.
The black monument bore the names of every Rank.
The white monument displayed a ranking list.
Legendary Grade...
Supreme Grade...
Quasi Sage...
Sage...
What immediately caught Daniel’s attention was that...
Every single first-place position bore the exact same name.
Dustin.
Daniel couldn’t help glancing at him.
Dustin simply smiled before pointing toward the black monument.
"This one measures Rank."
"Just place your hand on it."
"Think about whichever Rank you wish."
"It’ll suppress your strength to exactly that level."
He then pointed at the white monument.
"This one records the highest score."
"It only displays the champion of each Rank."
Daniel nodded.
Walking forward, he placed his palm upon the black monument.
Almost immediately...
A cool sensation flowed through his fingertips.
He focused his thoughts on the Legendary Grade.
Boom!
An invisible force poured into his body.
In an instant, his Divine Sovereign aura was completely suppressed.
His cultivation rapidly descended until it stabilized at the Legendary Grade.
Watching from nearby, Dustin’s eyes filled with anticipation.
"You can challenge any of the trials ahead."
Daniel nodded before walking toward the testing grounds beyond the monument.
A gigantic boulder floated before him.
A short explanation had been engraved upon its surface.
The trial itself was remarkably simple.
Carry the stone to the summit of the mountain...
And prevent it from rolling back down.
That alone counted as success.
"That’s it?"
Although he spoke lightly...
Daniel knew the trial couldn’t possibly be that straightforward.
Without hesitation, he activated his strength.
The enormous boulder—heavy beyond imagination—rose steadily into the air.
Then he began walking up the mountain path.
At first...
Everything proceeded smoothly.
Every step was steady.
Every movement effortless.
But halfway up the mountain...
An invisible force suddenly crashed into him from ahead.
With each additional step...
The boulder seemed to grow dozens of times heavier.
Daniel merely smiled.
Boom!
The Immortal Singularity ignited instantly.
With effortless ease...
He completely overwhelmed the opposing force.
Continuing upward...
His robes fluttered wildly in the mountain winds.
Before long...
He stood only ten steps away from the summit.
By now...
The resisting force had reached an astonishing intensity.
It felt as though the weight of the entire mountain rested upon his shoulders.
Yet Daniel didn’t even furrow his brow.
Applying just a little more strength...
He steadily placed the massive boulder upon the summit.
Watching from afar...
Dustin wasn’t particularly surprised.
Faustus had never known defeat.
In Dustin’s eyes...
Faustus was already far stronger than he himself had ever been at the same stage.
However...
The true difficulty of this trial wasn’t the climb.
Another restriction existed at the summit.
The instant the boulder reached the top...
It would automatically begin rolling back down the mountain.
When Dustin had completed the trial years ago...
He had relied upon his mastery of spatial formations to dismantle the restriction before finally succeeding.
So now...
How would Faustus solve this problem?

Soon afterward, the two of them passed through layer after layer of sacred domains before arriving at a vast, tranquil expanse.
The air itself carried an ancient, solemn atmosphere.
At the center of the grounds stood two enormous stone monuments.
One was black.
The other white.
They stood opposite one another like the boundary between day and night.
The black monument bore the names of every Rank.
The white monument displayed a ranking list.
Legendary Grade...
Supreme Grade...
Quasi Sage...
Sage...
What immediately caught Daniel’s attention was that...
Every single first-place position bore the exact same name.
Dustin.
Daniel couldn’t help glancing at him.
Dustin simply smiled before pointing toward the black monument.
"This one measures Rank."
"Just place your hand on it."
"Think about whichever Rank you wish."
"It’ll suppress your strength to exactly that level."
He then pointed at the white monument.
"This one records the highest score."
"It only displays the champion of each Rank."
Daniel nodded.
Walking forward, he placed his palm upon the black monument.
Almost immediately...
A cool sensation flowed through his fingertips.
He focused his thoughts on the Legendary Grade.
Boom!
An invisible force poured into his body.
In an instant, his Divine Sovereign aura was completely suppressed.
His cultivation rapidly descended until it stabilized at the Legendary Grade.
Watching from nearby, Dustin’s eyes filled with anticipation.
"You can challenge any of the trials ahead."
Daniel nodded before walking toward the testing grounds beyond the monument.
A gigantic boulder floated before him.
A short explanation had been engraved upon its surface.
The trial itself was remarkably simple.
Carry the stone to the summit of the mountain...
And prevent it from rolling back down.
That alone counted as success.
"That’s it?"
Although he spoke lightly...
Daniel knew the trial couldn’t possibly be that straightforward.
Without hesitation, he activated his strength.
The enormous boulder—heavy beyond imagination—rose steadily into the air.
Then he began walking up the mountain path.
At first...
Everything proceeded smoothly.
Every step was steady.
Every movement effortless.
But halfway up the mountain...
An invisible force suddenly crashed into him from ahead.
With each additional step...
The boulder seemed to grow dozens of times heavier.
Daniel merely smiled.
Boom!
The Immortal Singularity ignited instantly.
With effortless ease...
He completely overwhelmed the opposing force.
Continuing upward...
His robes fluttered wildly in the mountain winds.
Before long...
He stood only ten steps away from the summit.
By now...
The resisting force had reached an astonishing intensity.
It felt as though the weight of the entire mountain rested upon his shoulders.
Yet Daniel didn’t even furrow his brow.
Applying just a little more strength...
He steadily placed the massive boulder upon the summit.
Watching from afar...
Dustin wasn’t particularly surprised.
Faustus had never known defeat.
In Dustin’s eyes...
Faustus was already far stronger than he himself had ever been at the same stage.
However...
The true difficulty of this trial wasn’t the climb.
Another restriction existed at the summit.
The instant the boulder reached the top...
It would automatically begin rolling back down the mountain.
When Dustin had completed the trial years ago...
He had relied upon his mastery of spatial formations to dismantle the restriction before finally succeeding.
So now...
How would Faustus solve this problem?

chapters.title: Chapter 407 -407-Banner of Destiny’s Judgment
paragraphs: "How would you deal with it, Faustus?"
Dustin muttered under his breath.
At the summit.
No sooner had Daniel set the massive boulder down than he sensed an almost imperceptible tremor beneath his feet.
The enormous stone began to sway gently, its edge slowly tilting toward the mountain path as though it would roll back down at any moment.
"Interesting."
A faint smile appeared on Daniel’s lips.
Instead of trying to hold the boulder in place, he simply raised his right fist.
Without any fancy technique or Sacred Art, he threw a straightforward punch straight into the stone.
BOOM!
The seemingly indestructible boulder instantly split apart.
Spiderweb-like cracks spread across its surface before—
Bang!
—it exploded into countless fragments that were immediately swept away by the mountain wind, scattering into the sea of clouds.
"If the stone no longer exists," Daniel said casually while dusting off his hands, "then naturally, it can’t roll down the mountain anymore."
At the same moment, the rankings on the white stone monument shifted.
A brand-new name replaced the previous record holder.
[Legendary Rank No.1: Faustus]
Dustin stared blankly at the scene.
After a long silence, he finally squeezed out a sentence.
"...You can clear it like that?"
That boulder was no ordinary object.
Back when he attempted the trial himself, he had also tried changing the mountain and the stone through brute force.
Needless to say...
He had failed miserably.
Daniel leisurely walked back down from the summit, clearly satisfied.
"Faustus, would you like to try the other trials as well?"
Dustin finally recovered from his shock.
"Sure."
Daniel nodded.
"I’d like to see the Supreme Rank trials."
He placed his hand on the black stone monument once more.
Buzz—
A far more majestic power surged into his body.
In an instant, his cultivation was suppressed to the Supreme Rank.
Behind him, the Cycle Divine Domain quietly unfolded.
At that very moment...
Every trial monument throughout the territories ruled by the Chaos Humans began to glow simultaneously.
An unfamiliar name suddenly climbed to the very top of multiple rankings.
"A powerhouse is challenging the Sanctum Trials!"
"Who is it? Someone’s breaking Dustin’s records one after another!"
"Legendary Rank... Supreme Rank... It’s Faustus!"
"The peerless genius who advanced straight to Divine Sovereign immediately after entering the Divine Grade!"
"He’s challenging the trial records of the Chaos Humans!"
"And... he’s clearing every single one!"
"Unbelievable!"
Daniel had no idea that his casual attempt had already caused an enormous sensation throughout the Chaos Humans.
His progress through the trials was unstoppable.
Each challenge became increasingly difficult.
Quasi Sage.
Sage.
Divine Radiant.
Divine Sovereign...
Yet regardless of the difficulty, Daniel shattered every record with overwhelming ease.
Within a remarkably short time, every record once held by Dustin had been replaced by a single name.
Faustus.
The entire process looked less like difficult trials...
and more like someone casually playing a game.
Watching from the sidelines, Dustin could only shake his head with a bitter smile.
"Holy shit...
As expected of you, Faustus."
As the greatest genius of the current Chaos Humans—someone nurtured by the entire race since childhood—even he had no choice but to admit complete defeat before Faustus.
Daniel slowly walked out of the trial grounds.
"That was actually pretty interesting."
"Ahem..."
Dustin coughed awkwardly.
"There was one thing I forgot to mention."
"Oh?"
Daniel looked over.
"Breaking a trial record comes with an additional reward."
His eyes immediately lit up.
"Well played, Dustin."
"If you’d told me earlier there were rewards, I would’ve taken things a bit more seriously."
Dustin froze.
Wait...
You mean you weren’t even trying just now?
After a brief silence, he spread his hands helplessly.
"Would it really have made any difference?"
"With your strength, breaking the records was inevitable."
"I merely wanted to leave you with a pleasant surprise."
Daniel asked expectantly,
"What are the rewards?"
"They’re distributed according to performance."
Dustin smiled.
"With the results you’ve achieved, you’ll most likely receive the highest-tier reward."
Before he had even finished speaking—
Whoosh!
A brilliant treasure light suddenly materialized before them.
Its crimson radiance instantly dyed the entire trial grounds blood-red.
Floating in midair...
was a blood-colored battle banner.
Ancient totems covered its surface, while every pattern quietly flowed with profound Law power.
Daniel examined it before nodding in satisfaction.
"This should be a Primordial Law Grade treasure."
"...Not bad."
His eyes flickered slightly.
"Not bad? Holy shit!"
Dustin stared at him in disbelief.
"Brother... do you even know what that thing is?"
"Does it have something special about it?"
Daniel asked curiously.
"This is one of the Ten Primordial Law Grade Sacred Relics of the Chaos Humans!"
"Banner of Heaven’s Fall!"
"Banner of Heaven’s Fall?"
Daniel carefully examined the blood-red banner as it fluttered gently in the air.
Dustin explained proudly,
"The Banner of Heaven’s Fall ranks among the Ten Primordial Law Grade Holy Relics of the Chaos Humans."
"Although it’s technically only Primordial Law Grade, every one of these ten Sacred Relics possesses power comparable to a Primordial Supreme Treasure."
"Oh?"
Daniel’s interest was immediately piqued.
"But that’s not the most important part."
Dustin grinned.
"The Banner of Heaven’s Fall can be divided into nine subsidiary banners, each controlled by a different cultivator."
"When all nine banners are deployed together, they form the Heaven’s Judgment Array."
"It is one of the Ten Supreme Grand Arrays of the Chaos Humans."
"The formation has been passed down since ancient times and possesses unimaginable power."
"According to legend, when the Heaven’s Judgment Array is deployed in its complete form, it can summon an Ancient Holy Spirit."
"An Ancient Holy Spirit..."
"...is an existence that surpasses even an Eternal Sage."
"It belongs to the level of the Great Universal Will itself."
"Although the summoned Holy Spirit is merely a projection..."
"...it can still elevate the strength of every participant in the formation by an entire cultivation realm."
"At your current Divine Sovereign Realm..."
"You should be able to summon the projection of a Divine Lord."
After hearing the explanation, Daniel smiled inwardly.
With his Millionfold Boost System, once this banner entered his hands...
its grade was destined to rise even further.
Keeping a calm expression, he silently sold the treasure to the system.
Ding!
A familiar notification echoed within his consciousness.
[Sale detected.]
[Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Congratulations! You have obtained the Primordial Supreme Treasure: Banner of Destiny’s Judgment!]
Once again, the system upgraded the treasure from Primordial Law Grade to the level of a Primordial Supreme Treasure.
Its appearance barely changed.
It remained the same blood-red battle banner, and even the ancient runes and totems upon its surface looked almost identical.
Yet the power hidden within...
was now worlds apart.
Daniel swiftly stored the banner away with a perfectly natural motion.
Dustin noticed nothing unusual.
"This is the first Primordial Supreme Treasure I’ve ever obtained."
A ripple of excitement stirred within Daniel’s heart.
When he had crossed the Chaos Star Sea aboard the Shield of Aegis, he had already witnessed firsthand the terrifying might of a Primordial Supreme Treasure.
Such artifacts were capable of traversing the Chaos Star Sea itself and suppressing entire regions of the cosmos.
And now...
he finally possessed his own.
Although it was not a purely offensive Sacred Artifact...
its rarity and value were no less astonishing.

chapters.title: Chapter 408 -408-A Green-Eyed Dustin
paragraphs: [Banner of Destiny’s Judgment (Primordial Supreme Treasure)]
Category: Formation Artifact
Requirement: Divine Grade
Rank: Primordial Supreme Treasure
Description:
When jointly wielded by nine powerful cultivators, it can summon the projection of an Ancient Holy Spirit.
The summoned projection possesses a cultivation realm two major ranks above the wielder.
Background:
Legend speaks of an ancient race known as the Holy Spirit Remnants, whose origins are deeply connected to the ancient legends hidden within the ancestral homeland of the Chaos Humans.

It is said that the Holy Spirit Remnants were born from the flesh and blood left behind after the fall of an Ancient Holy Spirit. Gifted in the art of battle from birth, they pioneered the ancestral lands of the Chaos Humans and proudly proclaimed themselves descendants of the Holy Spirits.
After countless generations of research by the Holy Spirit sages, they eventually created the Heaven’s Judgment Array.
This banner carries the very will of the Ancient Holy Spirit.
Daniel’s eyes immediately lit up.
Every Primordial Supreme Treasure was a unique existence within heaven and earth.
They could never be duplicated.
Their rarity was beyond imagination.
The Banner of Destiny’s Judgment belonged precisely to that category—a supreme treasure containing immeasurable power.
"It suits me surprisingly well."
Daniel silently calculated.
"I possess ninety-nine clones."
"I completely satisfy the activation requirements."
"When fighting powerful enemies, I can unleash this treasure’s full potential."
According to its description, the Ancient Holy Spirit summoned by the banner could appear two entire major realms above the user.
Moreover, the treasure itself would continue growing alongside its master.
If Daniel were to become a Divine Lord, then activating the banner would allow him to summon an Oracle Grade projection of the Ancient Holy Spirit.
"This treasure isn’t just useful in battle."
"It can also be used to comprehend combat techniques."
Daniel pondered inwardly.
The Ancient Holy Spirit was the supreme embodiment of the Path of Battle.
Studying its projection would allow one to gain insight into countless Laws, Sacred Arts, and the very essence of combat itself.
"When I eventually reach Oracle Grade..."
"If I’m a T7 Oracle, I can summon a T9 Ancient Holy Spirit."
"A T9 Oracle..."
The original Banner of Heaven’s Fall could only summon a projection one major realm above its wielder.
After receiving the Millionfold Boost, the upgraded version could now cross two major realms.
The qualitative leap left Daniel thoroughly satisfied.
"Faustus."
Dustin spoke with genuine admiration.
"I’m honestly jealous."
"I’ve coveted these treasures for ages, yet luck has never smiled upon me."
"You show up once and immediately obtain one."
"Tsk... I’m practically green with envy."
Naturally, Dustin assumed that the treasure Daniel had obtained inside the Holy See was simply another Primordial Law treasure.
He had no idea that the Ring of Destiny was actually a relic transformed from the Holy Spirit of an Eternal Sage, making it incomparably more valuable than an ordinary Primordial Supreme Treasure.
Daniel had never enjoyed showing off.
He simply smiled and said nothing.
"Dustin."
He suddenly grinned.
"Tell me, are there any other places where rewards can be earned?"
"Why don’t you take me around all of them?"
The color instantly drained from Dustin’s face.
"No!"
He waved both hands frantically.
"There really aren’t any more!"
"You’re so stingy."
Daniel burst into laughter at Dustin’s horrified expression.
"I’m not an Astral Corsair."
"What are you so afraid of?"
No...
Those star-sea predators aren’t nearly as terrifying as you...
Dustin sighed inwardly before forcing a helpless smile.
Of course, Daniel was only joking.
The Chaos Humans had already bestowed enormous benefits upon him.
To Daniel, the Ring of Destiny alone was worth far more than everything else combined.
As for the Banner of Destiny’s Judgment, it was his very first Primordial Supreme Treasure.
He was already more than satisfied.
Nor was he in any hurry to complete the [Chaos Starfire] mission.
The mission required him to occupy an entire star system.
Without overwhelming strength, even if he managed to conquer one...
he would never be able to defend it.
After all, no true powerhouse would tolerate someone below Oracle Grade monopolizing an entire star system.
"In the end..."
"My strength is still insufficient."
Daniel quietly reflected.
He had an increasingly strong feeling...
that the opportunity for his next breakthrough lay within the Ring of Destiny.
Rather than rushing into the mission...
he might as well focus entirely on cultivation first.
Once he crossed that next threshold, he could worry about everything else afterward.
Daniel did not remain among the Chaos Humans for long.
Dustin personally escorted him beyond the borders of the Wisteria Star River.
"Why are you leaving so soon?"
Dustin asked.
"Are you uncomfortable staying in our territory?"
"Not at all."
Daniel smiled.
"I’d actually be perfectly happy freeloading here with the Chaos Humans."
"It’s just that..."
"I can feel my next breakthrough approaching."
Dustin immediately felt another crushing blow to his confidence.
You only broke through recently!
And now you’re about to advance again?
Back when they first met, both of them had stood at the peak of the Demi Sage realm.
Now...
Dustin had only reached Divine Radiant.
Meanwhile, Faustus had already become a Divine Sovereign...
and was somehow preparing to break through yet again.
The distance between them was only growing wider.
Faustus truly isn’t a normal person...
Dustin silently composed himself before speaking sincerely.
"Then I wish you a successful breakthrough."
"Thank you."
Daniel nodded.
The Imperial Bow Ark continued sailing through Chaosverse.
Meanwhile, Daniel extended his consciousness into the Ivahpin World.
That mysterious space could be entered no matter where he happened to be.
While wandering through Ivahpin World, he quickly noticed a newly posted mission related to Chaosverse.
The reward wasn’t particularly generous.
Yet it immediately caught his attention.
Companion Recruitment
A public sacred land has appeared within the Pyroflare Star River, Blooming Starfield, and Azurebird Star System of Chaosverse.
Seeking one companion for joint exploration.
Reward: 10,000 Contribution Points.
"A sacred land?"
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
Having cultivated the Law of Destiny, he could already vaguely sense that his breakthrough opportunity was connected to the Ring of Destiny.
He had been planning to search for a place rich in energy where he could cultivate.
However, he knew very little about Chaosverse.
Without guidance, he’d simply be wandering aimlessly.
Unexpectedly...
such an opportunity had appeared before him.
It would save him considerable effort.
He immediately accepted the mission and obtained the publisher’s contact information.
"Greetings."
A deep voice sounded from the other side of the Ivahpin Scroll.
"I am Thorne, a Divine Descendant of the Golden Holy Mountain."
"Hello."
Daniel calmly introduced himself.
"I am Faustus, a Divine Sovereign."
"A Divine Sovereign?"
Thorne was just about to decline.
After all, Divine Sovereigns generally lacked the qualifications necessary to survive within that sacred land.
Competition there would inevitably lead to fierce battles.
However...
the instant he heard the final word—
Faustus—
his attitude changed completely.
"My heavens!"
"Faustus?!"
"I never imagined it would be you!"
"What an unexpected surprise!"
Within the Golden Holy Mountain, that name had long become legendary.
Back when he was only a Demi Sage, he had already been recognized as the strongest Demi Sage in the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
Many even considered him the strongest Demi Sage in all known universes.
After advancing to the Divine Grade, he had leaped directly to the Divine Sovereign Realm.
Not long ago, he had shattered records on the Sky Trial Platform, earning treatment normally reserved for Quasi Oracle experts.
Those achievements had already spread throughout the Golden Holy Mountain by word of mouth.
Among those with even the slightest insight...
everyone understood one undeniable truth.
Faustus possessed limitless potential.
