chapters.title: Chapter 440 -440-Saving Them Twice
paragraphs: Although Daniel had already realized that the prince represented an opportunity for him, the young man had not yet truly fallen into a desperate situation.
If Daniel acted now, he would be unable to maximize the benefits.
Therefore, he decided to remain on the sidelines for the moment and quietly observe how the situation developed.
At the same time, he could sense that he was far from the only realm-crosser hiding within the city.
Countless experts of similar strength were concealed throughout the shadows, silently watching the conflict unfold.
Daniel paid them no attention.
His gaze remained firmly fixed upon the luxuriously dressed prince and his entourage.
The imperial guards protected the prince all the way toward the outskirts of the city.
However, none of them realized that a vast number of black-clad assassins had already laid an inescapable net beyond the city walls.
Daniel stood upon a distant rooftop and watched everything unfold.
His figure flickered continuously as he followed the group, ensuring that they never left his sight.
At the same time, he carefully restrained his aura so that none of them would detect his presence.
"Your Highness, I will do everything in my power to ensure that you escape alive!"
A peak Divine-grade expert suddenly erupted with terrifying Origin energy, blasting several black-clad assassins out of the way.
Behind him, the young man dressed in luxurious robes spoke with a resolute expression.
"Don’t worry, Chief Steward Foster. We will survive this."
"This assassination was most likely ordered by Prince Kaden. He has secretly colluded with several groups of outsiders."
"However, even he would not dare attack us openly within the Imperial City."
"We may face even greater danger once we leave the city."
"Besides, even if we somehow escape today, there will still be nowhere for us to go afterward."
Chief Steward Foster immediately became anxious.
"Your Highness, you’re being foolish!"
"You carry the imperial bloodline of the Eternal Empire. How could you be allowed to perish here?"
"Even if you must die, you should die within the imperial palace!"
"We need to leave this place immediately."
Hidden in the darkness, Daniel’s ears twitched slightly.
He had clearly heard them refer to the young man as a prince.
Golden light immediately flashed within his eyes as a plan formed in his mind.
If he saved this man, he would naturally obtain a legitimate opportunity to enter the Holy See.
It appeared that his earlier judgment had been correct.
This prince was indeed his greatest opportunity.
By now, the prince and his entourage had been completely surrounded by the black-clad assassins.
They appeared to have fallen into an inescapable situation.
Daniel felt that the timing was finally right.
He decisively raised one hand and summoned a surge of Origin power.
"It’s time for me to act."
As soon as he finished speaking, the phantom of a terrifying star river spread from his palm.
Within moments, it fully condensed into an enormous palm formed from Origin starlight.
The colossal hand descended from the sky.
The instant it made contact with the assassins, every black-clad figure was reduced to dust.
They were crushed out of existence by the enormous palm.
Yet the prince and his guards, despite standing in the middle of the attack, remained completely unharmed.
As dust filled the air, Chief Steward Foster and Prince Dorek both froze in shock.
They immediately activated their defenses, fearing that they might be struck by another attack.
While they were still filled with confusion, the dust in the distance gradually dispersed, revealing Daniel’s figure.
They instantly realized that this man had been the one who saved them.
Chief Steward Foster was the first to place one hand against his shoulder and bow respectfully.
"Thank you for saving our lives, Your Excellency."
"May I ask how we should address you?"
Prince Dorek also cupped his hands and expressed his gratitude.
"Thank you, Senior."
"May I ask where you come from?"
Faced with their questions, Daniel merely waved his hand.
"I am nothing more than a wandering traveler."
"While passing through your lands, I sensed an unusual disturbance within the city and came to investigate."
"I did not expect to encounter such shameless bullies preying upon the weak."
"I acted merely because I wished to."
"There is no need for you to remember my name."
"Perhaps we will meet again someday."
As soon as his words fell, Daniel’s figure rapidly faded from where he stood.
He did not even give the two men another opportunity to thank him.
Chief Steward Foster stared at the place where Daniel had disappeared, admiration immediately appearing on his face.
"That man sought neither wealth nor power, nor did he desire fame."
"He performed such a virtuous deed purely according to his own principles."
"Truly admirable."
Prince Dorek was equally emotional.
"That Senior’s strength is genuinely unfathomable."
"If we could obtain his assistance, there would probably be no uncertainty whatsoever in the struggle for the throne."
However, Chief Steward Foster shook his head and sighed.
"Unfortunately, Your Highness, that man appears accustomed to living freely."
"He is also indifferent toward fame and fortune."
"I fear he would never be willing to involve himself in the political struggles of our Holy See."
Dorek could only let out a long sigh.
He then quickly departed from the area.
Prince Kaden’s assassins were still hunting them, so preserving their lives naturally remained their highest priority.
They soon relocated to another tavern.
The establishment was situated within the slums, where very few people would think to search for them.
Prince Dorek had already changed out of his luxurious clothing and was now dressed in an ordinary coarse linen shirt.
He looked no different from someone who had grown up in the slums.
Along the way, they avoided countless inspections by the guards.
They also encountered another group of assassins, but Chief Steward Foster dealt with them all.
The two remained hidden inside the tavern for some time before preparing to return to the imperial palace.
However, the moment they revealed themselves, another group of black-clad assassins suddenly appeared.
The two leading assassins had even reached Sacred Marquis-grade!
Clearly, they had been lying in wait inside the tavern for quite some time.
The moment Dorek and Foster appeared, the assassins surrounded them completely.
"Dorek, you should obediently accept your death."
One of the assassins let out a sinister laugh.
Prince Dorek immediately shouted in fury,
"You wretched lackeys!"
"I never imagined that my elder brother would show so little regard for our familial bonds."
"He even sent assassins like you to murder a direct descendant of the imperial family."
"How utterly ruthless!"
The assassin gave another sinister chuckle.
"Once you are dead, what imperial bloodline will remain?"
"The struggle for the throne has always been a matter of life and death."
"You are destined to die here today."
With that, the assassin prepared to unleash his Origin power and kill Dorek.
However, at that moment—
An even more terrifying Origin pressure suddenly descended.
Before the two assassins could react, they and all their subordinates were crushed into nothingness.
Dorek and Chief Steward Foster both froze.
Only then did they realize that a familiar figure had appeared upon a nearby rooftop at some unknown moment.
It was Daniel—the same man who had saved them not long ago.
Dorek watched as Daniel slowly descended before them.
His face immediately filled with delight.
"Senior, it seems the two of us truly share an extraordinary fate."
"You have already saved me twice!"
Dorek was still young and failed to notice anything unusual about the situation.
However, a trace of suspicion appeared deep within Chief Steward Foster’s eyes.
Every time they fell into a desperate situation, this man appeared at precisely the right moment and effortlessly saved them.
All of this seemed far too coincidental.
Still, after considering that Daniel had shown them no hostility and had even repeatedly intervened to rescue them, Foster gradually formed a theory.
He silently felt a surge of relief on the prince’s behalf.
"It appears that Prince Dorek has finally found a powerful benefactor of his own."

chapters.title: Chapter 441 -441-Entering the Holy See
paragraphs: With that thought in mind, Chief Steward Foster took the initiative to recruit Daniel on the prince’s behalf.
"Senior, even in the Imperial City, your strength must rank among the very best."
"If you do not find our company beneath you, would you be willing to accompany us into the imperial palace?"
"The man beside me is Prince Dorek, one of the direct descendants of the Eternal Empire’s imperial family."
"If you are willing to assist us, we will certainly reward you generously."
Beside him, Dorek looked at Daniel with eyes full of anticipation.
With such an unparalleled expert at his side, he would never again need to worry about his safety when traveling outside.
However, Daniel deliberately declined.
"You two are overthinking matters."
"I was merely staying nearby for a short while. I happened to encounter you and saved you in passing."
"The affairs of the imperial family are far too complicated. I have no desire to become involved."
Dorek hurriedly attempted to persuade him.
"Senior, since you are traveling to experience the world, why not accompany us into the Holy See and witness the splendor of the imperial court?"
"Even if you care nothing for rewards, surely the experience itself would still be worthwhile?"
Experience it?
Daniel’s thoughts shifted slightly.
Prince Dorek was rather clever.
He had found a convincing excuse to draw Daniel into his faction.
Even after Daniel deliberately rejected him, Dorek had not given up. Instead, he had offered a reason that allowed both sides to continue cooperating without embarrassment.
Then again, Dorek was not blind to Daniel’s strength.
Although Daniel appeared to possess only Divine-grade cultivation, just like Chief Steward Foster, someone capable of crushing all opponents within the same Rank was exceptionally rare.
Even the Oracle-grade experts inside the imperial palace were less useful to Dorek than Daniel.
After all, those Oracle-grade generals obeyed only his father, not him.
Only an expert who was truly willing to follow him could be considered strength that genuinely belonged to him.
Naturally, Dorek was unwilling to let Daniel slip through his fingers.
Since the situation had already developed this far, Daniel decided to go along with it.
"Experience it for myself..."
"That does sound like a good idea."
"Very well. I will accompany you into the Holy See for the time being."
Chief Steward Foster and Prince Dorek finally breathed sighs of relief.
They had genuinely feared that Daniel might reject them outright.
Now that this peerless expert had agreed to join them, the safety of their future journeys had instantly increased by dozens of times.
With Daniel protecting them, the group returned to the imperial palace without further incident.
However, the current political situation was extremely sensitive, so they did not publicize the assassination attempt against Prince Dorek.
They would undoubtedly seek revenge later.
If they exposed the incident now, they might instead give their enemies leverage to use against them.
Mutual assassination between princes had practically become a tradition of the Eternal Empire.
Even the current Eternal Emperor had survived repeated life-and-death struggles against the other princes before finally reaching his present position.
After returning to the palace, the group kept an extremely low profile, behaving as though nothing had happened outside.
During this period, Daniel remained close to Dorek as his personal protector.
However, his attention was not focused entirely on guarding the prince.
Now that he had entered the Holy See, he began searching for channels through which he could obtain more information.
Unfortunately, the Holy See maintained extremely strict defenses against outsiders.
Even though Daniel had saved a prince, he was still unable to gain access to much valuable intelligence.
After remaining quiet for several days, Prince Dorek finally lost his patience.
Late one night, he prepared to sneak out with Chief Steward Foster.
However, Daniel stopped them directly and rejected their plan.
"I haven’t gone outside in ages."
"If I remain trapped here any longer, I’m going to lose my mind."
Prince Dorek looked at Daniel almost pleadingly.
Daniel still shook his head firmly.
Just as Chief Steward Foster was about to speak in Dorek’s defense, Daniel suddenly continued,
"What I mean is that with me here, there is no need for you to sneak out in the middle of the night."
"Even if you march out in broad daylight while beating drums and gongs, you will have nothing to fear."
"If assassins appear, I will deal with them."
Dorek and Foster were immediately overwhelmed by the absolute confidence in Daniel’s voice.
They had never imagined they would encounter an expert so certain that he could look down upon every enemy beneath the heavens.
Dorek agreed without hesitation.

Daniel could not resist asking,
"Where exactly are you planning to go?"
Dorek answered casually,
"We intend to visit the Fated Human Race."
Daniel’s face immediately revealed his surprise.
"You’re going to the Fated Human Race?"
As expected, the Fated Human Race truly existed in this world.
Dorek gave him a puzzled look before answering as though it were obvious.
"Of course."
"The Fated Human Race is where my mother was born and raised."
"Their clan leader is also my maternal grandfather."
"If I remember correctly, my uncle should currently be handling most of the clan’s affairs."
"However, the Fated Human Race resides within the Destiny Star System, which is some distance from here."
"That is why we need to depart early."
Chief Steward Foster added solemnly,
"Compared with the imperial palace, the Destiny Star System is Prince Dorek’s true stronghold."
"As long as we can reach it quickly, we will no longer need to fear the assassins dispatched by Prince Kane."
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"You are that confident?"
Chief Steward Foster patted his chest.
"Of course."
"The Fated Human Race possesses numerous Oracle-grade powerhouses and directly rules the entire Destiny Star System."
"As long as Prince Dorek returns there and receives their support, not only will his safety be guaranteed, but he will also have an opportunity to compete for the imperial throne in the future."
Daniel was not particularly convinced.
If the Fated Human Race were truly that powerful, they would not be confined to the Destiny Star System.
Nor would the Eternal Empire currently be ruled by its present Emperor.
Suddenly, Daniel remembered something.
During his stay in the palace, he had gathered some information regarding the Eternal Emperor.
He immediately asked,
"There is something I would like to know."
"I heard that the Eternal Emperor is preparing to advance and intends to undergo the Eternal Tribulation."
"If he fails to survive it, will he be reduced to tribulation ash?"
Chief Steward Foster’s expression shifted slightly.
Still, he nodded.
"That matter is already an open secret, so there is no harm in telling you."
"However, His Majesty is extremely sensitive about it. You had better not discuss it with others."
Daniel nodded before asking another question.
"Does that mean the various princes are currently slaughtering one another, eliminating every factor that might hinder their eventual entry into the imperial palace?"

chapters.title: Chapter 442 -442-The Fated Human Race
paragraphs: "That’s right. The imperial palace is in complete chaos right now."
Prince Dorek was the one who answered.
After all, he had only recently survived an assassination attempt ordered by another prince.
Dorek continued calmly,
"Prince Kane believes that he has the support of a great power behind him. More than half of the princes have already fallen victim to his schemes."
"Yet even that isn’t enough for him. He has gone completely mad and continues eliminating ’unnecessary’ princes like me."
"The Imperial City has become the most dangerous place in the world for us."
"Several of my brothers whom I knew personally have already died at his hands."
"That is why Chief Steward Foster and I planned to secretly flee the imperial palace late at night."
"If I continue staying here, who knows when another group of assassins might suddenly break in and kill me?"
So that was what had happened.
After hearing the full explanation, Daniel finally understood the entire sequence of events.
However, he merely sneered inwardly.
"It seems this fellow is even more foolish than I thought."
With that thought, Daniel suddenly changed his tone.
"If you intend to flee, then I will no longer help you."
The expressions of Prince Dorek and Chief Steward Foster changed drastically.
"Why?"
Daniel answered calmly,
"Because if you choose to abandon the imperial palace—the center of power—at this moment, you will inevitably lose any chance of ascending the throne in the future."
"That is why I advise you not to leave."
"You should remain within the Imperial City."
Prince Dorek looked deeply worried.
"But Prince Kane’s influence within the Imperial City is far too great."
"We possess no power to oppose him."
"So what if we lose our opportunity?"
"At the very least, we can survive within the Destiny Star System and preserve a sliver of hope."
Daniel shook his head.
"You are both mistaken."
"What Prince Kane wants most is for all of you to leave the Imperial City immediately."
"Of course, the best solution from his perspective would be to assassinate every one of you. That is why so many princes have recently died within the imperial palace."
"However, if the surviving princes voluntarily flee the Imperial City and return to the territories controlled by their maternal clans, that would serve as his second-best solution."
"Once you return to your maternal faction, you will have no choice but to live quietly and wait."
"Then, one day, you will receive the news that Prince Kane has ascended the throne of the Eternal Empire."
"If you attempt to raise an army against him afterward, you will become rebels in the eyes of the world."
"You will have surrendered the moral and political advantage before the conflict even begins."
Prince Dorek looked troubled.
"But my mother’s faction is not weak."
"Even if we raise an army to resist him, we may not necessarily be at a disadvantage."
"Wrong."
Daniel shook his head and immediately refuted him.
"Your best option is to remain within the imperial palace and closely observe Prince Kane and the other factions."
"At the same time, you must recruit more experts and secretly cultivate a force that belongs entirely to you."
"If the Emperor truly perishes during his advancement, that will be the moment when every prince and faction makes their move to seize the throne."
"What I have described is not merely your best option."
"It is your only path to survival."
"Otherwise, you will never have another opportunity to return to the imperial palace."
"You will only be able to watch helplessly as Prince Kane ascends the throne."
After Daniel’s explanation, realization gradually appeared on the faces of Dorek and Foster.
Neither of them was a fool.
Both were exceptionally shrewd, and they immediately understood his meaning.
As a prince, Dorek’s greatest advantage was his presence within the imperial palace.
Even if he obtained the support of the Fated Human Race, what could he actually do with it?
He could not openly dispatch an army to eliminate the other princes and then attack the imperial throne itself.
That was absolutely impossible.
Setting aside whether the Fated Human Race possessed enough strength, the act of raising an army in rebellion alone would give his enemies all the justification they needed.
If Dorek lost, he would be branded a traitor forever.
Even his descendants would lose any possibility of inheriting an imperial title.
Their original plan—to retreat into the territory of the Fated Human Race and wait for an opportunity—was likewise a dead end.
Once Prince Kane ascended the throne, the princes wandering outside and hiding within their maternal territories would inevitably be purged one after another.
Even if they somehow survived, they would spend the rest of their lives under confinement, never permitted to leave their own territories.
Therefore, if Dorek wished to preserve both his life and freedom, he had only one option.
He had to remain within the imperial palace and compete against the other princes for the throne.
To compete for the throne, he had to stay at the center of power.
And to remain close to the center of power, he had no choice but to stay within the palace.
No matter how they considered the matter, Daniel’s path was indeed the safest and most reasonable.
With that realization, Prince Dorek’s gaze became resolute.
"In that case, we will remain here."
"We will not go anywhere."
Chief Steward Foster nodded as well.
"That’s right. We should remain here and abandon the idea of leaving."
Daniel nodded faintly.
In truth, Prince Dorek’s path had been fixed from the moment he was born.
He could only remain in the Imperial City and walk this seemingly endless road.
He had simply been unwilling to face that truth.
Daniel’s arrival and guidance had torn apart the illusion Dorek had hidden behind for so long.
With every avenue of retreat cut off, Prince Dorek was destined to embark upon the blood-soaked road of political struggle.
"Thank you, Senior Faustus."
"Your words have truly enlightened me."
"To me, you are no different from a second parent who has given me a new life."
Suddenly, Prince Dorek dropped to his knees with a thud.
"If Senior Faustus does not object, I wish to acknowledge you as my teacher and ask you to guide me."
"If I truly have the opportunity to ascend the throne in the future, I will never forget the wisdom and kindness you have shown me today."
Seeing this, Chief Steward Foster hurriedly knelt as well, his face filled with excitement.
"Senior Faustus, your words today have truly saved Prince Dorek’s future."
"You possess both extraordinary wisdom and unrivaled strength."
"Please remain and assist Prince Dorek in ascending the throne."
"With your support, His Highness will undoubtedly gain an overwhelming advantage."
"On the day he truly becomes Emperor, you will be revered by generations to come."
"You will become the Imperial Tutor—second only to the Emperor himself!"
Imperial Tutor?
Daniel blinked upon hearing the title.
That position seemed to perfectly overlap with the objective of his current mission.
Moreover, judging from the reactions of the two men before him, the timing was already right.
If he continued refusing, his behavior might begin to appear suspicious and instead arouse their doubts.
With that thought, Daniel raised his hands and helped the master and servant to their feet.
He deliberately let out a long sigh.
"I have never cared for fame, wealth, or power."
"However, since the two of you possess such sincere and grateful hearts, and Prince Dorek appears to have the potential to accomplish great things..."
"Then, for the sake of the people beneath the heavens, I shall temporarily emerge from seclusion."
"I will help them secure a wise and virtuous Emperor."

chapters.title: Chapter 443 -443-Entering the Struggle for Power
paragraphs: To better integrate himself into their group, Daniel deliberately delivered an impressive speech filled with noble sentiments.
At this moment, he brought out acting skills worthy of an award.
After all, this concerned the objective of his mission. He could not afford the slightest carelessness.
Prince Dorek and Chief Steward Foster were clearly deeply moved by his words, nodding repeatedly in agreement.
Daniel then continued,
"That said, the Fated Human Race is indeed a valuable source of support. We cannot simply abandon their assistance."
Prince Dorek already obeyed Daniel without question.
He hurriedly asked,
"Please enlighten me, Teacher."
Daniel nodded.
"Do not be impatient. Listen carefully."
"The current Eternal Emperor is a half-step Eternal powerhouse. His attempt to overcome the tribulation cannot possibly be completed within a short period."
"Even if he fails and begins to turn into tribulation ash, that process will still take time."
"During that period, we will need the assistance of the Fated Human Race."
At this point, Daniel turned toward Chief Steward Foster.
"Chief Steward Foster, if I remember correctly, you were also born into the Fated Human Race."
"You should return to the Destiny Star System immediately."
"If you travel alone, the enemy should be less likely to target you."
"Return to the Fated Human Race and bring back several experts, along with a large quantity of wealth and resources."
"The Imperial City is currently in a state of turmoil. Many paths can be opened with money."
"Without sufficient wealth, there is very little we can accomplish."
Chief Steward Foster strongly agreed and immediately nodded.
"Senior is absolutely correct. I will make the arrangements at once."
However, he soon looked toward Prince Dorek with some hesitation.
"But if I leave, then His Highness..."
Daniel smiled and waved his hand.
"Do not worry. I will watch over the Prince."
"You may leave without concern."
"You need only ensure your own safety."
"After all, I do not yet fully understand Prince Kane’s temperament."
"Although I believe he may not pursue you, no one can say for certain what he might do if he has truly gone mad."
"We will await your good news within the Imperial City."
Chief Steward Foster nodded.
His figure immediately flickered and vanished as he departed to request reinforcements from the Fated Human Race.
After Chief Steward Foster left, Daniel questioned Prince Dorek about the various structures and districts within the current Imperial City.
This information would be extremely useful for his future plans.
According to Dorek, the Imperial City was actually an independent planar space.
Although it appeared to stand upon the surrounding wilderness, the city and the outside world had long since been separated into two distinct regions.
Without imperial blood or permission from the guards stationed at the city gates, entering it was virtually impossible.
Furthermore, the plane could expand at any moment.
Once fully expanded, it would become even larger than an entire star system.
In Daniel’s memory, perhaps only the headquarters of the Golden Holy Mountain could compare with a plane of this scale.
Although undercurrents were surging throughout the Imperial City, its security had grown even stricter.
The Eternal Emperor was preparing to undergo his tribulation, so every defensive measure had been raised to the highest level.
After explaining the situation, Prince Dorek asked impatiently,
"Teacher, are you planning to take action now?"
Chief Steward Foster had already departed, and Dorek had only recently survived an assassination attempt.
At present, he desperately wanted to take some action to calm his nerves.
Daniel answered calmly,
"There is no need to rush."
"We will wait until Chief Steward Foster returns with a group of veteran retainers."
"Once he brings back reinforcements and wealth, there will be far more we can accomplish."
"Our influence within the Imperial City is currently far too weak."
"We need a great deal of money to buy informants and turn them into our eyes and ears."
"Prince Dorek, the first lesson you must learn if you wish to become Emperor is patience."
After hearing Daniel’s instruction, Prince Dorek drew in a deep breath and obediently answered,
"I understand, Teacher."
Daniel then asked for more information regarding the Eternal Emperor.

It turned out that although the Eternal Emperor was a peak half-step Eternal powerhouse who had ruled this universe for countless years, even the strongest existence would eventually face a tribulation.
Furthermore, Great Dao tribulation clouds existed throughout this realm.
The stronger a person became, the more rapidly signs of tribulation-ash corruption would emerge.
As the supreme powerhouse of the empire, the Eternal Emperor now faced only two possible outcomes.
He could take the final step, successfully overcome the tribulation, and attain the position of an Eternal Lord.
Or he could fail, be reduced entirely to tribulation ash, and have his Divine Soul destroyed.
Throughout history, the Eternal Emperor had fathered several hundred children.
However, one hundred and eighty of them had died under mysterious circumstances for various reasons.

Among the remaining hundred or so descendants, only seven princes truly possessed the qualifications to inherit the throne after considering their talents, bloodline purity, and various other factors.
Each of those seven princes was now supported by a major faction.
If the Eternal Emperor fell one day, the seven would inevitably wage a brutal struggle to seize the throne.
The first was Prince Alvin.
Behind Prince Alvin stood an enormous faction within the Holy See.
Several trusted ministers of the Holy See’s Elder Council shared close blood ties with him.
His birth mother also wielded considerable influence within the imperial harem.
His faction was undoubtedly a force that could not be underestimated.
The second was Prince Silas, Prince Alvin’s biological younger brother.
However, the two brothers did not stand together.
Their relationship had always been hostile.
Prince Silas was currently serving in one of the Eternal Empire’s military legions.
It was said that he was now attempting to leave active service and return to the Imperial City.
After operating within the army for many years, he had already established a powerful military background.
The third was Prince Felix.
Behind him stood the largest merchant organization in the empire—the Eternal Chamber of Commerce.
Its wealth was virtually immeasurable.
The fourth prince was Felix’s biological brother, Lucian.
He was currently cultivating within the Oracle Hall.
Among the seven heirs, he possessed the highest cultivation Rank and the greatest personal strength.
At present, he had already reached Divine-grade.
The power supporting him naturally required little explanation.
It was the Oracle Hall itself.
The Oracle Hall was the highest military institution within the entire empire.
Even the Eternal Emperor treated it with caution and respect.
Most of the empire’s Oracle-grade experts were gathered within the Oracle Hall.
From first-stage experts all the way to T9 powerhouses, experts of every level could be found there.
Most importantly, Prince Felix and Prince Lucian shared an exceptionally close relationship.
Together, the two brothers represented an overwhelmingly powerful faction.
As for the fifth heir, it was naturally Prince Kane—the man who had recently dispatched assassins after Dorek.
Several major factions stood behind Prince Kane as well.
Although their combined influence was slightly inferior to that of the Oracle Hall, they still possessed enormous power.
Unlike the Oracle Hall, which received constant attention from the imperial family and was regarded warily by every faction, Prince Kane’s supporters enjoyed far greater freedom.
Moreover, each of them was completely loyal to him and devoted to helping him ascend the throne.
It was precisely because of this support that Prince Kane could hunt down other members of the imperial family as he pleased without being held accountable.

He hurriedly asked,
"Please enlighten me, Teacher."
Daniel nodded.
"Do not be impatient.
Listen carefully."
"The current Eternal Emperor is a half-step Eternal powerhouse.
His attempt to overcome the tribulation cannot possibly be completed within a short period."
"Even if he fails and begins to turn into tribulation ash, that process will still take time."
"During that period, we will need the assistance of the Fated Human Race."
At this point, Daniel turned toward Chief Steward Foster.
"Chief Steward Foster, if I remember correctly, you were also born into the Fated Human Race."
"You should return to the Destiny Star System immediately."
"If you travel alone, the enemy should be less likely to target you."
"Return to the Fated Human Race and bring back several experts, along with a large quantity of wealth and resources."
"The Imperial City is currently in a state of turmoil.
Many paths can be opened with money."
"Without sufficient wealth, there is very little we can accomplish."
Chief Steward Foster strongly agreed and immediately nodded.
"Senior is absolutely correct.
I will make the arrangements at once."
However, he soon looked toward Prince Dorek with some hesitation.
"But if I leave, then His Highness..."
Daniel smiled and waved his hand.
"Do not worry.
I will watch over the Prince."
"You may leave without concern."
"You need only ensure your own safety."
"After all, I do not yet fully understand Prince Kane’s temperament."
"Although I believe he may not pursue you, no one can say for certain what he might do if he has truly gone mad."
"We will await your good news within the Imperial City."
Chief Steward Foster nodded.
His figure immediately flickered and vanished as he departed to request reinforcements from the Fated Human Race.
After Chief Steward Foster left, Daniel questioned Prince Dorek about the various structures and districts within the current Imperial City.
This information would be extremely useful for his future plans.
According to Dorek, the Imperial City was actually an independent planar space.
Although it appeared to stand upon the surrounding wilderness, the city and the outside world had long since been separated into two distinct regions.
Without imperial blood or permission from the guards stationed at the city gates, entering it was virtually impossible.
Furthermore, the plane could expand at any moment.
Once fully expanded, it would become even larger than an entire star system.
In Daniel’s memory, perhaps only the headquarters of the Golden Holy Mountain could compare with a plane of this scale.
Although undercurrents were surging throughout the Imperial City, its security had grown even stricter.
The Eternal Emperor was preparing to undergo his tribulation, so every defensive measure had been raised to the highest level.
After explaining the situation, Prince Dorek asked impatiently,
"Teacher, are you planning to take action now?"
Chief Steward Foster had already departed, and Dorek had only recently survived an assassination attempt.
At present, he desperately wanted to take some action to calm his nerves.
Daniel answered calmly,
"There is no need to rush."
"We will wait until Chief Steward Foster returns with a group of veteran retainers."
"Once he brings back reinforcements and wealth, there will be far more we can accomplish."
"Our influence within the Imperial City is currently far too weak."
"We need a great deal of money to buy informants and turn them into our eyes and ears."
"Prince Dorek, the first lesson you must learn if you wish to become Emperor is patience."
After hearing Daniel’s instruction, Prince Dorek drew in a deep breath and obediently answered,
"I understand, Teacher."
Daniel then asked for more information regarding the Eternal Emperor.

It turned out that although the Eternal Emperor was a peak half-step Eternal powerhouse who had ruled this universe for countless years, even the strongest existence would eventually face a tribulation.
Furthermore, Great Dao tribulation clouds existed throughout this realm.
The stronger a person became, the more rapidly signs of tribulation-ash corruption would emerge.
As the supreme powerhouse of the empire, the Eternal Emperor now faced only two possible outcomes.
He could take the final step, successfully overcome the tribulation, and attain the position of an Eternal Lord.
Or he could fail, be reduced entirely to tribulation ash, and have his Divine Soul destroyed.
Throughout history, the Eternal Emperor had fathered several hundred children.
However, one hundred and eighty of them had died under mysterious circumstances for various reasons.

Among the remaining hundred or so descendants, only seven princes truly possessed the qualifications to inherit the throne after considering their talents, bloodline purity, and various other factors.
Each of those seven princes was now supported by a major faction.
If the Eternal Emperor fell one day, the seven would inevitably wage a brutal struggle to seize the throne.
The first was Prince Alvin.
Behind Prince Alvin stood an enormous faction within the Holy See.
Several trusted ministers of the Holy See’s Elder Council shared close blood ties with him.
His birth mother also wielded considerable influence within the imperial harem.
His faction was undoubtedly a force that could not be underestimated.
The second was Prince Silas, Prince Alvin’s biological younger brother.
However, the two brothers did not stand together.
Their relationship had always been hostile.
Prince Silas was currently serving in one of the Eternal Empire’s military legions.
It was said that he was now attempting to leave active service and return to the Imperial City.
After operating within the army for many years, he had already established a powerful military background.
The third was Prince Felix.
Behind him stood the largest merchant organization in the empire—the Eternal Chamber of Commerce.
Its wealth was virtually immeasurable.
The fourth prince was Felix’s biological brother, Lucian.
He was currently cultivating within the Oracle Hall.
Among the seven heirs, he possessed the highest cultivation Rank and the greatest personal strength.
At present, he had already reached Divine-grade.
The power supporting him naturally required little explanation.
It was the Oracle Hall itself.
The Oracle Hall was the highest military institution within the entire empire.
Even the Eternal Emperor treated it with caution and respect.
Most of the empire’s Oracle-grade experts were gathered within the Oracle Hall.
From first-stage experts all the way to T9 powerhouses, experts of every level could be found there.
Most importantly, Prince Felix and Prince Lucian shared an exceptionally close relationship.
Together, the two brothers represented an overwhelmingly powerful faction.
As for the fifth heir, it was naturally Prince Kane—the man who had recently dispatched assassins after Dorek.
Several major factions stood behind Prince Kane as well.
Although their combined influence was slightly inferior to that of the Oracle Hall, they still possessed enormous power.
Unlike the Oracle Hall, which received constant attention from the imperial family and was regarded warily by every faction, Prince Kane’s supporters enjoyed far greater freedom.
Moreover, each of them was completely loyal to him and devoted to helping him ascend the throne.
It was precisely because of this support that Prince Kane could hunt down other members of the imperial family as he pleased without being held accountable.

chapters.title: Chapter 444 -444-The Situation Among the Factions
paragraphs: The sixth contender was Prince Marcus.
The power supporting Prince Marcus was the Holy See Academy, the highest educational institution in the empire.
His greatest backer was none other than the academy’s dean.
The dean’s students could be found throughout every corner of the Eternal Empire, and he himself possessed an extraordinary status within the Holy See.
In terms of foundation and influence, Prince Marcus’s faction was not inferior to Prince Kane’s in the slightest.
As for the final contender, it was naturally Prince Dorek.
Behind Prince Dorek stood the Fated Human Race.
Although the Fated Human Race occupied only a single star system within this world, countless experts could be found among its people.
Its current clan leader, the Auric Divine Emperor, was an incomparably terrifying peak T9 Oracle-grade expert.
There was even a high possibility that he had concealed his true strength and had actually reached the half-step Eternal Rank.
Moreover, he simultaneously commanded the Eternal Legion—the most powerful and mysterious military force in the entire Eternal Empire!
This was the current situation surrounding the seven imperial princes of the Eternal Empire.
As for the remaining hundred or so princes, none of them possessed the qualifications to compete against these seven for the throne.
Their strength and backgrounds were far inferior.
Naturally, they had no hope whatsoever of challenging the seven leading contenders.
After hearing all this, Daniel finally gained a general understanding of the seven princes and the current political situation within the Eternal Empire.
"Judging from this, Prince Dorek possesses the weakest faction of the seven."
Daniel understood the situation clearly.
Among the seven princes, the one with the greatest strength and deepest foundation was Prince Lucian.
If Lucian obtained the full support of both the Oracle Hall and his biological brother, his chances of seizing the imperial throne would surpass those of every other prince.
In terms of wealth, he also possessed the support of the Eternal Chamber of Commerce.
No one could possibly compete with him financially.
In terms of military strength, no faction could rival the Oracle Hall either.
At least on the surface, Prince Lucian was undoubtedly the most powerful contender.
Prince Alvin ranked second.
Although Alvin appeared relatively unremarkable, he was actually the prince closest to the center of political authority.
To put it simply, his connections among the empire’s highest officials were far stronger than those of the other princes.
As for the remaining contenders, most were relatively evenly matched and did not warrant much further attention.
Only a few days later, Chief Steward Foster returned safely.
Just as Daniel had predicted, because Prince Dorek had not traveled with him, Foster had not attracted the attention of the assassins dispatched by Prince Kane.
The moment he returned, Foster brought excellent news.
He had successfully persuaded the Fated Human Race to send Oracle-grade experts.
He had also brought back an enormous quantity of wealth and resources.
All those resources had been quietly delivered to Prince Dorek’s residence without drawing anyone’s attention.
The entire operation had been exceptionally discreet.
Daniel immediately hurried to the palace.
The moment he entered, he saw a mountain of radiant treasures piled before him.
The dazzling light was so intense that he could not help narrowing his eyes.
He turned toward the smiling Chief Steward Foster.
"How many experts did you bring back?"
"And where are they now?"
Chief Steward Foster quickly answered,
"Sir, I followed your instructions and explained the full severity of the situation to the Fated Human Race."
"Once I made the consequences clear, the clan—which had initially been somewhat hesitant—decisively chose to support Prince Dorek."
"They abandoned all their previous concerns and reservations."
"They directly dispatched one T7 Oracle-grade expert, six T6 Oracle-grade experts, and ten fifth-stage Oracle-grade experts."
Foster’s face filled with admiration as he continued,
"With such overwhelming military support, Prince Dorek will no longer need to fear assassination."
"We may even take the initiative and launch a counterattack to exact revenge."
When Daniel had first instructed Foster to request reinforcements from the Fated Human Race, many had believed the mission impossible.
After all, the Fated Human Race had always been unwilling to interfere in the empire’s internal affairs.
However, Foster had explained that if Prince Dorek successfully seized the imperial throne, the Fated Human Race would obtain immeasurable merit and rewards.
Furthermore, the karma involved in this struggle was no less significant than an immeasurable Heavenly Tribulation.
Nearly every powerful being would inevitably be drawn into this enormous vortex of conflict.
The stronger a faction was, the more impossible it became for them to avoid involvement.
After all, this concerned the future direction of the entire empire.
As a major power, the Fated Human Race had already been bound to Prince Dorek’s cause.
Their only path to survival was to support him with everything they possessed.
Otherwise, if he failed, the entire race might face extermination.
Prince Kane was no merciful man.
The moment he ascended the throne, he would undoubtedly purge the maternal clans of his former brothers.
He would never permit any surviving prince to retain the possibility of rebelling against him.
Prince Dorek was the nephew of the current clan leader of the Fated Human Race.
Their blood relationship was exceptionally close.
If the clan refused to support Dorek, they would inevitably be targeted during the future purge.
Their fates were already intertwined.
If one prospered, both would prosper.
If one fell, both would suffer.
Chief Steward Foster had repeated Daniel’s entire analysis without leaving out a single detail.
The members of the Fated Human Race immediately became deeply worried.
In the end, they had no choice but to agree to support Prince Dorek.
After hearing Foster’s report, a faint smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
"Those Oracle-grade experts naturally had to come here and assist us."
"Since they have arrived, assign them to protect Prince Dorek."
"As for this enormous quantity of wealth..."
Daniel turned toward Chief Steward Foster and issued another instruction.
"Use all of it to buy every informant and official who can be bought."
"Make certain they become our eyes and sources of intelligence."
"You may also attempt to contact spies currently serving the other factions."
"Everyone beneath the heavens acts for the sake of profit."
"Even if they currently serve another prince, they can still be purchased as long as we offer sufficient resources."
"Pay particular attention to those holding positions within the Imperial City, as well as the generals responsible for the city’s defenses and other critical locations."
"They will be able to provide us with an enormous amount of assistance."
"Chief Steward Foster, you should be highly experienced in such matters."
"You have also lived within the Imperial City for many years."
"I believe you are sufficiently reliable."
"You should be able to handle all of this properly, correct?"
After speaking, Daniel fixed Chief Steward Foster with an intense gaze, waiting to see how he would respond.
The moment Foster felt Daniel’s piercing stare, he was struck by a terrifying pressure—
A pressure he had previously experienced only when standing before the Emperor himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 445 -445-The Performance Begins
paragraphs: Under Daniel’s gaze, the elderly Chief Steward Foster could not help trembling from head to toe.
He felt as though he had been targeted by a giant python.
He hurriedly nodded.
"Rest assured, my lord. I will handle this matter properly."
A faint smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
"In that case, I will leave everything in your hands."
"You will have to work hard during this period. Try to put every arrangement into place."
"If everything is completed successfully, our influence within the Imperial City will finally be able to expand without restraint."
Prince Dorek watched as Daniel assigned every task, and for the first time, he experienced the sheer pleasure of having someone else manage everything on his behalf.
Ever since Daniel became his teacher, it felt as though he no longer needed to worry about anything.
It was almost as if he had found a true father.
Daniel gave him an overwhelming sense of security.
Before this teacher, who was like a father to him, every difficulty seemed capable of being resolved with ease.
However, as a prince, Dorek knew that he could not truly ignore everything.
If he handed every matter over to Daniel, then even if he eventually ascended the throne, he might soon be stripped of power and reduced to a puppet.
Dorek immediately asked,
"Teacher, what should we do next?"
Daniel waved his hand and answered calmly,
"Isn’t that obvious?"
"Our next step is to expand our influence and make our presence known within the imperial palace."
"Make our presence known?"
Prince Dorek was still unfamiliar with political maneuvering and immediately looked confused.
He could not understand why they should act conspicuously instead of keeping a low profile at such a sensitive time.
Daniel explained,
"Dorek, think carefully."
"His Majesty currently has several hundred children."
"Even if your identity is somewhat special, you are still only one of them."
"Imagine raising more than a hundred identical pets."
"If a few of them never display anything unique, do you think you would ever choose them over the others?"
"This principle has remained unchanged since ancient times."
"People will always pay more attention to those who make the most noise."
After hearing Daniel’s explanation, Prince Dorek suddenly understood.
He had never imagined that the struggle for power could be approached from such a perspective.
He immediately bowed and asked for further guidance.
"Teacher, in that case, how can we safely ensure that Father notices our presence?"
Daniel smiled and waved his hand reassuringly.
"The time has not yet come."
"There is no need to rush. Sooner or later, an opportunity will present itself."
Prince Dorek nodded, only partially understanding.
Several days later, inside the largest tavern in the Imperial City.
The establishment was packed with people.
The clinking of wine cups echoed everywhere, mingling with the rich scent of perfume and extravagant revelry.
Daniel and Prince Dorek had changed into ordinary clothing and quietly appeared on the top floor.
The area had already been reserved in advance and had effectively belonged to them throughout this period.
Daniel looked out the window.
All manner of patrols moved continuously through the streets below.
A faint smile appeared on his lips as he turned toward the prince behind him.
"Your Highness, the performance we arranged is about to begin."
"The role you will play is extremely important."
"You must not make any mistakes."
Prince Dorek smiled confidently and patted his chest.
"Don’t worry, Teacher."
"I have rehearsed it countless times. I will follow the original plan exactly."
"Besides, with you here, even if I make a mistake, it probably won’t cause too much trouble, right?"
Daniel’s expression turned serious.
"If you ruin this performance, even I will not be able to clean up the consequences."
"You must ensure that nothing goes wrong."
Prince Dorek immediately nodded solemnly.
At the same time, in a corner on the lower floor of the tavern, Chief Steward Foster—also wearing a disguise—finally met his informant.
He stared coldly at the revealingly dressed woman before him.
"Villar, I have already paid you an enormous amount."
"You had better not attempt any tricks."
"As long as you follow the original plan and die when the time comes, everything I promised will immediately be delivered to the location you designated."
"But if anything unexpected happens, you know what the consequences will be."
The woman before him was named Villar.
She was a well-known dancer within the tavern, but she also secretly worked as an informant for several different factions.
Chief Steward Foster had uncovered her identity not long ago.
He had immediately spent a vast sum to buy her cooperation, all for the sake of carrying out the upcoming plan.
Villar’s expression became anxious.
She hurriedly nodded.
"Rest assured, my lord. I have already memorized every part of the plan."
"Everything will proceed exactly as you instructed."
Chief Steward Foster nodded and gestured toward the stairs.
"You may go up now."
Villar immediately headed upstairs.
The enormous tavern had nine floors and was crowded everywhere.
Following the route she had memorized, she soon reached the second floor and entered a private room.
Not long afterward—
Boom!
A deafening explosion suddenly erupted from within the room.
Countless patrons were startled.
They put down their wine cups and turned toward the private room.
At the same time, Daniel heard the commotion from the top floor.
He immediately nodded toward Prince Dorek, who had been waiting for this moment.
"It is time for you to enter the stage."
Prince Dorek drew in a deep breath.
Pretending to be curious, he deliberately raised his voice.
"Teacher, something appears to have happened downstairs."
"Why don’t we go and take a look together?"
Daniel also responded loudly,
"Very well. Let us go down and see what happened."
The two walked downstairs openly and arrived at the private room on the second floor where the incident had occurred.
By now, the entrance had been completely surrounded by spectators.
Even many outsiders had joined the crowd and were heatedly discussing what had happened inside.
"What is going on?"
"The Grand Commander of the City Defense Army committed such a despicable act in broad daylight?"
"This has truly opened my eyes!"
"That man is a complete monster!"
"If he wanted a woman, then so be it—but he actually beat Villar to death!"
"She was the goddess of this tavern!"
"What a pervert!"
"He committed such a vile act and then tried to silence the witness by killing her."
"How can someone like him be a general of the Holy See?"
"He is a disgrace to the Eternal Empire!"
Under the deliberate encouragement of several planted agitators within the crowd, the atmosphere had already transformed into one of public condemnation.
At that moment, Prince Dorek appeared among the gathered spectators.
Following Daniel’s plan, he immediately raised his voice.
"Everyone, make way."
"I am Prince Dorek of the imperial family."
"What exactly happened here?"
"Allow me to investigate."

Prince Dorek drew in a deep breath.
Pretending to be curious, he deliberately raised his voice.
"Teacher, something appears to have happened downstairs."
"Why don’t we go and take a look together?"
Daniel also responded loudly,
"Very well.
Let us go down and see what happened."
The two walked downstairs openly and arrived at the private room on the second floor where the incident had occurred.
By now, the entrance had been completely surrounded by spectators.
Even many outsiders had joined the crowd and were heatedly discussing what had happened inside.
"What is going on?"
"The Grand Commander of the City Defense Army committed such a despicable act in broad daylight?"
"This has truly opened my eyes!"
"That man is a complete monster!"
"If he wanted a woman, then so be it—but he actually beat Villar to death!"
"She was the goddess of this tavern!"
"What a pervert!"
"He committed such a vile act and then tried to silence the witness by killing her."
"How can someone like him be a general of the Holy See?"
"He is a disgrace to the Eternal Empire!"
Under the deliberate encouragement of several planted agitators within the crowd, the atmosphere had already transformed into one of public condemnation.
At that moment, Prince Dorek appeared among the gathered spectators.
Following Daniel’s plan, he immediately raised his voice.
"Everyone, make way."
"I am Prince Dorek of the imperial family."
"What exactly happened here?"
"Allow me to investigate."

chapters.title: Chapter 446 -446-The Plan Succeeds
paragraphs: The moment Dorek announced his identity, the surrounding crowd erupted into an uproar.
This was the busiest hour of the day, and the tavern was the largest establishment in the entire Imperial City.
Many officials of the Holy See were also drinking and gathering with their friends here.
The moment they saw Dorek, they immediately recognized him.
Their expressions became excited as they hurried forward to bow, while ordering the surrounding patrons to clear a path.
"This is wonderful! I never expected to encounter Prince Dorek here."
"With His Highness present, he will definitely uphold justice for us!"
"That Grand Commander of the City Defense Army is no human being at all! He committed such a morally depraved act. The imperial family must punish him severely!"
"Your Highness, you must not let him escape!"
"But isn’t it inappropriate for a prince to suddenly interfere in a case like this?"
"Shouldn’t the Imperial Capital Inspectorate be responsible for handling it?"
"Are you an idiot?"
"The Grand Commander of the City Defense Army is already a subordinate of the Imperial Capital Inspectorate. If you let them investigate this case, they will undoubtedly protect one another!"
Hearing the voices rising from the crowd, Dorek seized the opportunity to speak.
"Everyone, please listen to me."
"I have come only to serve as a witness. I do not intend to personally take control of this case."
"It would still be more appropriate for the relevant authorities to conduct the official investigation."
His statement sounded fair and impartial without provoking the anger of the crowd.
The surrounding people immediately voiced their agreement.
"That’s right! This is how the matter should be handled."
"His Highness only needs to remain here as a witness. The law-enforcement authorities can deal with everything afterward."
"With a member of the imperial family placing pressure upon them, the Inspectorate probably won’t dare shield its own subordinate."
"Exactly. That commander definitely won’t escape punishment."
Hidden among the crowd, Daniel silently observed everything.
He looked into the private room and saw that the scene inside was exactly as he had planned.
The room was already in complete disarray.
Villar’s body lay motionless upon the bed, seemingly devoid of all life.
Beside the bed stood the Grand Commander of the City Defense Army.
He was utterly flustered, his face as red as a monkey’s backside, and his entire body trembled as he attempted to explain himself.
The corners of Daniel’s lips rose into a faint smile.
The plan had succeeded perfectly.
Villar had been a famous dancer and singer at this tavern.
Both the wine she had consumed and the medicinal incense burning inside the private room contained special substances capable of magnifying a person’s desires without limit.
The Grand Commander had obviously drunk the same wine.
Combined with the effects of the incense, he had naturally entered a state in which he could no longer control himself.
Once he began committing the crime, Villar followed the original plan.
She created an enormous disturbance and then decisively took her own life, giving the commander no opportunity to react or defend himself.
He had been caught red-handed.
Once the commander was arrested because of this incident, the other city-defense officials whom Dorek had already bribed could quickly rise through the ranks and replace him.
And this was merely the first step of Daniel’s plan.
The second step would begin once the causal connection involving the Imperial Capital Inspector was established.
After that came the third and ultimate objective—
Increasing Prince Dorek’s presence within the imperial palace.
Had Dorek not appeared at the tavern or interfered in the matter, this would have looked like nothing more than an insignificant case of an official abusing and killing a common woman.
But now, Dorek had appeared before countless witnesses and personally involved himself in the case.
It would naturally attract the Emperor’s attention.
After all, Dorek was one of the few princes with a genuine possibility of inheriting the throne.
Now, he had suddenly inserted himself into a major case capable of causing an uproar throughout the entire city.
Even a blind man would be forced to take notice.
Furthermore, following Daniel’s earlier instructions, Dorek had already bribed several eunuchs within the Holy See.
Those eunuchs had always controlled the flow of rumors and private gossip throughout the imperial court.
With a little manipulation surrounding this case, they might cause the entire Holy See to pay far greater attention to Prince Dorek.
Another important factor was public sentiment.
A prince had personally stepped forward to seek justice for an innocent common woman who had been driven to death by a military commander.
Anyone hearing the story would immediately believe that Dorek was an upright, honorable, and virtuous prince.
It would allow him to establish the perfect image of a wise and righteous future ruler.
Once such an image took root among the common people, it would be extremely difficult to destroy.
When the hearts of the people gradually turned toward him, Dorek’s reputation among the public would naturally far surpass that of the other princes.
Admittedly, using the life of a dancer to build this entire plan was somewhat cruel.
But exchanging a single life for so many benefits was undeniably worthwhile.
Besides, Villar had not had long to live in the first place.
She had contracted several contagious diseases.
According to her original trajectory of fate, she would most likely have died either in prison or from her illnesses sooner or later.
By dying early now, she could at least preserve a degree of dignity and secure an enormous payment for her family.
After considering all of this, Daniel pulled his thoughts back and turned his gaze toward Dorek.
Everything now depended on whether the prince could continue performing according to plan.
At this moment, Dorek had already pushed through the crowd and arrived before the private room.
He stared coldly at the panicked commander and spoke in an indifferent voice.
"I am Prince Dorek of the Eternal Empire."
"You have just committed an unforgivable and depraved crime."
"You have therefore forfeited your right to freedom."
"Remain here and wait for the City Defense Bureau to send officers to arrest you."
In truth, hundreds of incidents were occurring throughout the Imperial City at this very moment.
Some districts had suddenly caught fire.
Others had reported thefts or large-scale street brawls.
Enormous shipments of goods had inexplicably vanished, causing traffic to become blocked across several major roads.
Furthermore, flying and traveling above the permitted speed were both forbidden within the Imperial City.
Every single disturbance had been arranged for the sake of this seemingly ordinary case inside the tavern.
Chief Steward Foster had already followed Daniel’s instructions and prepared everything outside.
For a short period, the City Defense Bureau would have no possibility of sending anyone here to investigate the truth.
Inside the private room, the Grand Commander’s face turned ashen the moment he heard Dorek’s name.
He hurriedly looked toward the subordinates and fellow officials he knew inside the room, silently begging them for help.
At the same time, he shouted that he had been wronged.
"Your Highness, I have been framed!"
"The wine was drugged! I wasn’t acting under my own will—I was being controlled!"
"If you don’t believe me, you can ask my subordinates and colleagues!"
"They witnessed the entire incident!"
The commander had finally realized the severity of the situation.
To avoid imprisonment, he could only insist that he had been drugged and had therefore lost control of himself.
What he did not know was that every colleague standing beside him—
Had already been bought by Prince Dorek.

chapters.title: Chapter 447 -447-Raising His Profile
paragraphs: The pitiful commander still had no idea that his colleagues had already been bought by Dorek.
In fact, they had secretly contributed to creating this enormous commotion from the very beginning.
They had coveted the position of Grand Commander of the City Defense Army for a long time.
Now that a prince had personally offered them a ladder to climb, they naturally welcomed the opportunity. They wanted nothing more than to see their commander thrown into prison.
Sure enough, the moment Herschel turned to them for help, his colleagues immediately changed their stories.
"Bullshit, Herschel!"
"You were clearly overcome by lust and tried to assault that dancer. None of us could stop you!"
"Still, we bear some responsibility. As your colleagues and subordinates, we should have done everything possible to restrain you."
"Unfortunately, your Strength far surpassed ours. In the end, we failed to stop you."
Another official immediately added,
"Everyone here drank the same wine as Herschel."
"None of us experienced any problems, yet Herschel claims the wine somehow controlled his mind."
"How could that possibly be true?"
After hearing the words of his own colleagues and subordinates, the commander’s face turned deathly pale.
He stared in horror at these suddenly unfamiliar men, then at Dorek, who was watching him with a faint smile.
At that moment, he finally understood.
This entire incident had been a trap designed specifically for him.
Just as he prepared to shout out his discovery, a uniformed officer from the City Defense Bureau suddenly drew a weapon from his waist.
"Damn you! You fraudulent prince dared frame my lord!"
"Everyone in the Imperial City knows that my lord maintains excellent relations with many princes."
"You must be an impostor!"
"My lord, I will follow your orders and cut down this false prince!"
The words that had gathered in the commander’s throat immediately froze.
He stared blankly at the man’s actions, cold sweat pouring down his forehead.
What did he mean?
Where had this man even come from?
Herschel did not know him at all!
And when had he ever claimed to have excellent relations with the various princes?
What exactly was this lunatic trying to accomplish?
As the officer drew his weapon and lunged toward Dorek, the surrounding crowd immediately erupted into chaos.
At that moment, Daniel stepped forward and shouted furiously,
"You traitorous scum! You dare attack a prince?"
The instant his words fell, Daniel struck out with his palm.
The force of the blow was incomparably imposing, instantly piercing straight through the Grand Commander’s chest.
After all, Herschel was only a Divine Radiant expert.
How could he possibly withstand an attack from Daniel, who could casually kill even T7 Oracle-grade experts?
Under that single palm strike, the commander’s aura vanished completely.
He died on the spot inside the private room.
At the same time, the subordinate who had pretended to attack Dorek hurriedly dropped his weapon.
His entire body trembled as he began wailing.
"Please spare me, great expert!"
"You must spare my life!"
"The commander forced me to act. I had no choice!"
"I never truly wanted to attack His Highness!"
"That’s right, my lord!"
"We barely knew the commander. He merely invited us here to drink."
"We never imagined he would turn out to be such a monster!"
The commander’s colleagues and subordinates inside the private room all dropped to their knees and begged for mercy.
With only a few sentences, they completely confirmed both accusations against their former superior—
Assaulting and killing an innocent woman, and attempting to assassinate a prince.
The spectators cried out in satisfaction upon witnessing this scene.
They immediately began praising Daniel.
"That commander actually harbored treasonous intentions!"
"He even tried to kill a prince!"
"When Prince Dorek saw the man charging toward him, his expression didn’t change at all."
"He didn’t retreat even half a step. Such courage is truly admirable!"
"Fortunately, this expert intervened."
"Prince Dorek must possess extraordinary fortune. Without this expert, he might have been killed by that commander on the spot!"
The agitators hidden among the spectators immediately spoke up, skillfully steering the crowd’s emotions.
Sure enough, under their influence, the surrounding people began shouting with righteous fury.
Not only did they completely ignore the fact that Daniel had casually killed an imperial official, but they also condemned the dead commander as a disgrace beyond redemption.
All manner of insults and curses erupted from the crowd.
Every furious word became another tool for shaping Dorek’s public image.
As for the small number of silent observers, they were naturally officials of the Holy See.
They watched everything unfold without speaking.
Their instincts, sharpened through many years in officialdom, told them that the entire incident carried the unmistakable scent of conspiracy.
However, suspicion was only suspicion.
Their impression of Dorek still changed slightly.
No matter how the matter had been arranged, the prince had clearly demonstrated an excellent political mind.
Meanwhile, the other incidents occurring throughout the city were gradually resolved.
The arsonists responsible for the fires were arrested.
The thieves involved in the robberies were also captured.
Only after being delayed for quite some time did the officials of the City Defense Bureau finally arrive at the tavern.
After learning what had happened from the surrounding witnesses, the commanding officer immediately dismounted and knelt on one knee before Dorek.
"Your Highness, since you personally witnessed the incident, we must ask you to accompany us and provide a statement."
Dorek naturally agreed.
With an elegant and composed smile, he replied,
"That man committed countless vile acts."
"Since I personally witnessed the matter, I should naturally assist you in solving the case."
Everything continued according to the script Daniel had prepared.
Dorek had participated in nearly every stage of the incident.
As long as he remained perfectly involved in each development, his presence and reputation would inevitably rise significantly afterward.
Daniel, as the man who had killed the criminal commander, was naturally also invited to the City Defense Department.
The surrounding crowd was quickly dispersed.
Daniel and Dorek followed the commanding officer to the department’s headquarters.
The moment they entered, the officer personally guided them toward the office of the Imperial Inspector.
The Inspector was responsible for all security and patrol operations throughout the Imperial City.
The City Defense Bureau was merely one of the departments directly under his authority.
Before long, they arrived at his office.
The Inspector personally rose to welcome them.
He repeatedly expressed concern for Dorek’s safety and well-being, yet barely mentioned the commander Daniel had killed.
This proved that the money they had spent earlier had already produced results.
The plan had been executed perfectly.
The moment they returned to the residence, Prince Dorek could no longer maintain his composed act.
An excited smile appeared across his face.
"Teacher, your plan was simply flawless!"
"We actually succeeded!"
Daniel waved his hand.
"This is not yet the time to celebrate."
"What happens next depends on how the Inspector handles the matter."
"If he follows the original plan and reports everything to the Emperor, your reputation throughout the Imperial City—and even the entire Holy See—will rise dramatically."

chapters.title: Chapter 448 -448-Sweeping Across the Entire City
paragraphs: After bidding farewell to the Inspector, the two soon returned to the prince’s residence.
The moment they entered a secret chamber shielded by an array, Dorek could no longer contain his excitement.
"Teacher, this is wonderful!"
"We succeeded!"
Dorek had remained extremely nervous throughout the entire operation.
They had not been given any opportunity to rehearse. Their first attempt had been the real performance.
Now that everything had proceeded so smoothly, he could finally breathe a sigh of relief.
Daniel saw through the young man’s thoughts and waved his hand slightly.
"Don’t celebrate too soon."
"This is only the beginning."
His eyes flickered.
"That City Defense Inspector is definitely a clever man."
"He will know exactly what to do."
Prince Dorek froze for a moment before instinctively asking,
"What do you mean?"
Daniel explained,
"It’s simple."
"If the Inspector handles the case according to official procedure, he will be required to report the incident to the Emperor."
"Since that is the case, he will naturally hope that you suppress the matter and minimize its impact."
"After all, you personally intervened, while the official who caused the scandal belonged to his City Defense system."
"If the incident becomes too serious, it will inevitably damage his reputation, future prospects, and opportunities for promotion."
"Therefore, we only need to remain silent and avoid drawing further attention."
"That alone will accomplish our purpose."
"Afterward, once he owes us a favor, he will naturally have to speak well of us before the Emperor."
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
"Furthermore, he must promote all the hidden agents we planted within the City Defense Department."
"At the very least, he will have to quietly permit one of our people to take over the dead commander’s position."
"Once that happens, our influence will have successfully extended into the Holy See’s Inspectorate system."
"At that point, regardless of what the Inspectorate itself believes, under the current struggle between the seven princes, they will already have one foot inside our camp."
"Whether they acknowledge it or not, they will effectively have chosen a side."
Dorek immediately became thrilled upon hearing this.
Within the Holy See’s power structure, the City Defense Inspectorate was practically half of the political core!
If they could obtain the support of the Imperial City Inspectorate, then even if they exhausted an enormous amount of wealth, the exchange would still be extraordinarily worthwhile.
"Teacher, your strategy is brilliant!"
"With the smallest possible price, we obtained the greatest possible benefit!"
Daniel smiled faintly.
"Heh. It was merely a minor trick."
However, he silently thought,
"With this, I should soon be able to use the merit of killing that corrupt official to obtain a formal position within the Holy See."
Strictly speaking, the position of Imperial City Inspector during this ancient era was roughly equivalent to commanding the imperial guard.
The safety of the entire Imperial City rested in their hands.
Therefore, the support of the City Defense Inspectorate was extremely important.
Whichever prince received their backing would immediately gain several additional chances of victory.
However, their current scheme had only temporarily drawn the Inspector closer to them.
Actually persuading the entire Imperial City Inspectorate to fully support Dorek would not be so easy.
Neither the timing nor the conditions were sufficient yet.
Still, the Imperial City Inspector possessed the privilege of directly meeting the Eternal Emperor.
There would likely be results within a short period.
When that time came, they would merely need to wait patiently and carry out a little more manipulation.
Dorek would use the incident to become one of the most discussed figures within the Holy See.
At the same time, Daniel’s official appointment would also be secured.
At that moment, Dorek looked toward Daniel expectantly and asked impatiently,
"Teacher, now that we have completed this mission, what should we arrange next?"
After experiencing the events of today, Dorek had become completely convinced of Daniel’s abilities.
He now eagerly awaited their next operation, hoping to advance even further.
Daniel answered calmly,
"There is no need to rush."
"If the Imperial City Inspector acts as promised, the Emperor will inevitably summon you personally."
"When that happens, you only need to follow my instructions and answer his questions appropriately."
"Afterward, you will no longer need to worry about your future."
"Your path will be bright and unobstructed."
Dorek was immediately intoxicated by Daniel’s encouraging words, and delight appeared across his face.
He quickly asked,
"Teacher, when Father questions me, how should I respond?"
"That is extremely simple."
"You only need to display the qualities expected of an excellent prince."
"For example, humility, caution, diligence, and a willingness to learn."
"If your acting skills are poor, then simply pretend to be an honest and straightforward man."
Daniel smiled.
"As long as you maintain that attitude, we will remain in an unbeatable position."
"The better you perform, the easier it will be to implement our future plans."
Dorek pondered for a moment.
"Does that mean that as long as I appear sufficiently intelligent, I will have a chance to inherit the throne?"
Daniel shook his head.
"No."
"Appearing too intelligent may not necessarily be a good thing."
Dorek looked confused.
"Why?"
Daniel explained,
"First, the moment His Majesty sees how calculating and capable you are, he will immediately sense your ambition toward the throne."
"He has not yet shown any clear signs of dying."
"At present, the thing he fears most is someone coveting his imperial position."
Dorek suddenly understood.
Daniel continued,
"Second, you will attract the united hostility of the other princes."
"Do not assume that the princes are truly as harmonious and affectionate as they appear in public."
"In reality, each of them may desire your death more than anyone else, all so that they can seize the throne for themselves."
"They would be delighted to see you fail and would mercilessly destroy your entire faction afterward."
Cold sweat began flowing down Dorek’s back.
He had never imagined that so many hidden considerations were involved.
Daniel continued,
"Therefore, for now, you must behave honestly."
"Or at the very least, you must appear honest."
"The more harmless you seem, the more the Emperor will trust and approve of you."
"If you attempt to act clever, you may instead lose his favor."
"In other words, the less you do and the less you say, the easier it becomes to prove that you are merely a straightforward and obedient prince."
"If you do nothing, you cannot make a mistake."
"Remember that truth."
Dorek was now completely convinced.
He had never considered any of these principles before.
After hearing Daniel explain them, he felt as though a veil had been lifted from his mind.
Daniel nodded faintly.
"Good."
"Since you understand, follow these instructions from now on."
Dorek’s face lit up.
He immediately rose and bowed deeply toward Daniel once again.
"Thank you for your guidance, Teacher."
"This student has benefited enormously!"
"With you guiding me, I will have nothing to fear for the rest of my life!"
"From this day forward, I will remember every word you have taught me and will never disappoint your expectations!"
Daniel merely shook his head slightly and responded with a meaningful smile.
At the same time—
Inside Prince Kane’s palace, Kane was listening to a subordinate’s report.
The subordinate bowed respectfully before recounting everything that had happened during the encounter with Dorek that day, along with all the subsequent developments.
